items.title: In an age of expanding reproductive horizons, a deeper mechanistic understanding of myoma-related infertility is essential.
items.key: Fibroids are the most commonly encountered benign tumours and their association with infertility has long been a source of controversy. Indeed, fibroids are increasingly observed in women seeking medical treatment for infertility due to extended reproductive horizons and the current trend for women to postpone childbearing. Growing numbers of studies and reviews are now highlighting the possible negative effects of fibroids on fertility and reproductive outcomes. The aim of this opinion paper is to provide an overview of mechanisms by which uterine fibroids could impair fertility, looking to open potential avenues for the development of targeted therapy.

items.title: Global Reproductive Carrier Screening Guidelines: A Scoping Review.
items.key: Documents were split between single-condition, targeted, and expanded carrier screening recommendations and focused on indications for RCS among preconception populations. Domain 5 ("Applicability") and Domain 3 ("Rigor of Development") had the lowest AGREE II scaled scores, at 23.7% and 30.3% respectively. This review highlights the inconsistencies among RCS guidelines, which likely contribute to observed disparities in what is offered by clinicians and healthcare systems. The poor methodological rigor of existing documents calls for a commitment to standardizing a framework for developing recommendations and promoting evidence-based care.

items.title: Surveillance strategies for the early detection of malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors in neurofibromatosis type 1: a systematic review.
items.key: One retrospective imaging study traced 91% of MPNSTs to a pre-existing distinct nodular lesion. Diffusion-weighted MRI and FDG-PET discriminated benign from malignant tumors with high sensitivity in symptomatic referral cohorts, with threshold-dependent specificity. Harms were inconsistently reported. Certainty was very low for surveillance impact and harms and low for diagnostic accuracy. Current evidence is insufficient to establish whether surveillance improves outcomes; this review informs the design of prospective trials and the next revision of international surveillance guidelines.

Overall, STING may represent a molecular link between mitochondrial damage and inflammation in PCOS, although predominantly preclinical evidence warrants further clinical investigation.

items.title: Prenatal Genetics and Investigational in Utero Gene Therapy for Sickle Cell Disease: Clinical, Ethical, and Justice Considerations.
items.key: There is currently no evidence that prenatal somatic gene therapy is cost-effective or would overcome access barriers. Its reliance on fetal medicine, molecular, and manufacturing infrastructure could initially widen disparities. Clinical translation would be ethically defensible only after disease-specific comparative evidence, independent oversight, non-directive consent, lifelong follow-up and a credible equitable-access plan. Strengthening newborn screening and proven care remains the immediate justice priority.

items.title: Placental abnormalities in congenital diaphragmatic hernia: A systematic review of experimental and clinical studies.
items.key: Fetal vascular malperfusion, thrombotic lesions, and chronic inflammation were reported at histology. Ex-vivo CDH fetoplacental arteries showed impaired function with excessive constriction and inadequate relaxation. Animal studies reported reduced placental weight, trophoblast injury and apoptosis, and altered retinoid metabolism. Despite extensive literature on CDH, the status of the placenta remains understudied. Available evidence indicates that CDH is associated with abnormalities involving fetal placental vascular pathology. Studies using standardized assessment are needed to define the role of the placenta in CDH and correlate its status with disease severity and neonatal outcomes.

items.title: A comparison of UK and French guidelines on the identification of pregnant women at low-risk of complications: a nationwide population-based study.

items.key: These studies were heterogenous in their reporting and overall have a level of evidence of 4. Ovarian conservation surgery was performed in 234/250 (94%) ovaries. Among those with documented follow-up (222/234, 95%), postoperative ultrasound demonstrated ovarian viability in 190/222 (86%). Delayed presentation and ischemic appearance did not reliably predict loss of function. Conclusion Ovarian conservation should be attempted in all cases of benign pediatric ovarian torsion, regardless of symptom duration or intraoperative appearance. Postoperative ultrasound within three months of detorsion is recommended to confirm ovarian viability and standardize follow-up care.

items.title: Sexual Violence/Abuse and Cervical Cancer: A Systematic Review of the Relationship.
items.key: Findings point to a need for prevention strategies that consider how gender intersects with exposure to sexual violence/abuse. The review also suggests elevated co-occurrence between cervical cancer and sexual violence/abuse relative to global population estimates (~10% intimate-partner violence and ~6% non-partner violence). Limitations include small samples and measurement heterogeneity. Findings support co-produced, survivor-centred and trauma-informed approaches to cervical cancer prevention and oncology care that address barriers to healthcare engagement. Larger studies using validated measures and confounder-aware designs are needed.

items.title: Peripartum infective endocarditis in complex congenital heart disease: Melody valve infection after caesarean delivery.
items.key: tpartum course of a 26-year-old nulliparous woman with repaired double outlet right ventricle, ventricular septal defect, and severe pulmonary stenosis who was managed by a multidisciplinary pregnancy heart team. Her postpartum course was complicated by suspected pulmonary embolism and infective endocarditis of a Melody valve, requiring right ventricle-pulmonary artery conduit replacement. This case highlights the diagnostic challenges of postpartum cardiopulmonary symptoms in women with complex congenital heart disease and raises important questions regarding infective endocarditis prophylaxis in women with prosthetic cardiac material.

In HGSC, the adjusted hazard ratio for OS from C-CAT registration was 1.19 (95% confidence interval=0.88-1.61; p=0.271) for Y220C…
CONCLUSION: TP53 Y220C was detected in approximately 4% of HGSCs. Neither survival nor co-alteration associations reached statistical significance, although the estimates were imprecise. These findings support direct mutation-level detection through comprehensive genomic profiling.

items.title: Guideline-practice gap in molecular subtyping and lynch syndrome screening for endometrial cancer.
items.key:
RESULTS: Adherence to routine MMR and p53 assessment was nearly universal at 98.5% (201/204) but significantly declined to 20.6% (42/204) when POLE status was…
CONCLUSION: Molecular classification remains limited by factors that likely reflect financial and institutional barriers restricting POLE testing, although its clinical utility was demonstrated by de-escalation of radiotherapy in a POLE-mutated patient. Similarly, the absence of MLH1 methylation triage renders Lynch syndrome screening non-selective, lowering germline testing completion rates. Addressing these real-world implementation gaps is critical to optimizing risk stratification and ensuring efficient diagnostic workflows.

items.title: Twenty-five-year trends and projections of gynecologic cancer incidence in Korea: findings from cancer registry data.
items.key:
RESULTS: In 2023, crude incidence rates of cervical, corpus uteri, and ovarian cancers were 14.5, 18.6, and 14.9 per 100,000 women, respectively. Corpus uteri and ovarian cancer incidence increased, whereas cervical cancer incidence declined. Corpus uteri cancer surpassed cervical cancer after 2020, followed by ovarian cancer. The increase in corpus uteri cancer was steeper among women aged 20-49 years than among those aged ≥50 years. Risks of corpus uteri and ovarian cancers were higher in recent birth cohorts than in the…
CONCLUSION: The burden of corpus uteri and ovarian cancers is expected to increase substantially, highlighting the need for effective prevention and management strategies.

items.title: Substantial but not focal lymphovascular space invasion independently predicts lymph node metastasis in uterine-confined endometrial cancer: implications for the FIGO 2023 staging system.
items.key:
RESULTS: Lymph node metastasis rates differed significantly across LVSI groups (4.7% for no LVSI, 6.7% for focal LVSI, and 40% for substantial LVSI; p<0.001). Substantial LVSI was independently associated with nodal metastasis (odds ratio=5.83; 95% confidence interval=2.75-12.35; p<0.001), whereas focal LVSI was not. Deep myometrial invasion, non-endometrioid histology, and cervical stromal invasion were also…
CONCLUSION: Substantial LVSI, rather than its mere presence, is independently associated with lymph node metastasis. These findings support the biological rationale of the FIGO 2023 staging system and highlight the importance of standardized LVSI reporting in clinical practice.

items.title: Ascites-derived interleukin-10 drives tumor invasion in advanced epithelial ovarian cancer via STAT3 and ERK1/2 signaling.
items.key:
RESULTS: IL-10 levels in malignant ascites varied markedly among patients (134.38±84.80 pg/mL) and were positively correlated with serum cancer antigen 125 levels (r=0.553, p=0.014), while no statistically significant association was observed between ascitic IL-10 levels and ascites volume (r=0.312, p=0.207).…
CONCLUSION: These findings identify IL-10 as a biologically relevant immunosuppressive mediator within the EOC ascitic microenvironment that contributes to tumor invasiveness through immune cell-tumor cell crosstalk. Targeting ascites-derived IL-10 may represent a potential microenvironment-modulating strategy for controlling malignant ascites and invasive behavior in advanced EOC.

items.title: Prognostic significance of peripheral serum inflammatory markers NLR and PLR in high-grade endometrial carcinoma: a multicenter retrospective study.
items.key:
RESULTS: NLR was identified as an independent risk factor for both recurrence and death, whereas PLR was an independent risk factor only for recurrence. We established nomograms for predicting disease-free survival and overall survival.
CONCLUSION: NLR and PLR are closely associated with the prognosis of patients with high-grade EC. Our novel prediction models can provide accurate postoperative risk stratification and prognostic prediction for this patient population.

items.title: Distinct clinical and prognostic features of cervical neuroendocrine carcinoma: a nationwide registry-based study.
items.key:
RESULTS: NEC accounted for 1.6% of registered cervical cancers. Median age at diagnosis was 48 years (range, 22-96). Pelvic LNM remained relatively low in T1A-T1B2 disease (8.3% in T1A-T1B1 and 12.4% in T1B2) but increased markedly in bulky tumors from T1B3 onward (37.3% in T1B3) and remained high in locally advanced tumors (44.4%-48.6% in T2B-T3B). Overall survival…
CONCLUSION: FIGO 2018 stages captured OS gradients in high-grade cervical NEC, but intermediate stages showed limited prognostic discrimination. Favorable outcomes in node-negative ≤IB2 disease and weak T-based stratification within IIIC1 suggest NEC-specific prognostic patterns distinct from common cervical histologic subtypes.

items.title: Effects of Artificial Intelligence Chatbot Interventions on Women during Pregnancy and Postpartum: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Six studies (four randomized controlled trials and two nonrandomized controlled trials) were included. Intervention themes included gestational diabetes, postpartum depression, well-being, maternal-fetal attachment, aneuploidy testing, and breastfeeding. Individual trials reported…
CONCLUSIONS: AI chatbot interventions show promise for improving maternal knowledge, self-efficacy, and attachment. However, the available evidence does not show consistent reductions in depression or anxiety. Large, rigorously designed studies are needed to refine intervention strategies, ensure equity, and establish a robust basis for integrating these interventions into maternal healthcare systems.

items.title: Beyond semen analysis: a systematic review of sperm CatSper dysfunction in male infertility and a proposed framework for functional assessments.
items.key: In reported cases of assisted reproductive technology, conventional in vitro fertilization was frequently associated with fertilization failure, whereas intracytoplasmic sperm injection often achieved favorable fertilization outcomes and pregnancies. Based on this evidence, we propose a multilevel assessment framework integrating phenotypic screening, physiological functional assays, and genetic testing. This framework should be regarded as a translational approach, rather than a validated diagnostic pathway. Larger prospective studies are required to establish standardized protocols, reference thresholds, and clinical utility.

items.title: Changes in Perinatal Management in Pregnancies With Abnormal Findings Detected on Ultrasound in the Late Second and Third Trimester.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 1116 referrals, advanced ultrasound confirmed an abnormal finding in 65.0% (725/1116): congenital anomalies (n = 266), abnormal biometry (n = 246), poly-/oligohydramnios (n = 104), and arrhythmia (n = 109). Invasive testing was performed in 2.5% (18/725), with abnormal results in six. Follow-up data were available for 96.6% (700/725), with a live birth…
CONCLUSION: Despite the absence of routine third-trimester ultrasound, abnormal late-pregnancy findings frequently alter perinatal management. These findings support offering all women a third-trimester scan that includes a standardized assessment of key anatomical structures to improve diagnostic consistency and equity of care.

items.title: Contraceptive decision-making in women with migraine: integrating guidelines, vascular risk, and clinical practice.
items.key: Evidence on progestin-only methods, particularly desogestrel, suggests potential improvement in migraine frequency, while data on newer formulations such as drospirenone remain limited. Practical algorithms integrating major and minor vascular risk factors can support individualized contraceptive counseling. Hormonal contraceptive choice in women with migraine requires balancing efficacy with vascular safety. CHCs are contraindicated in MA, while POCs represent the first-line option across most scenarios. For MO, low-dose CHCs may be cautiously considered in the absence of risk factors. Ongoing monitoring and individualized risk stratification are essential to safe decision-making.

items.title: Long-Term Postpartum Dyspareunia and Sexual Dysfunction After Childbirth.
items.key:
RESULTS: Twenty-two eligible reports representing 21 unique studies or cohorts were included; 2 randomized rehabilitation studies contributed to quantitative synthesis. Dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remained clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum, with incomplete recovery persisting in a substantial subset of women. Persistent morbidity was most…
CONCLUSIONS: Persistent dyspareunia and broader sexual dysfunction remain clinically relevant beyond 6 months postpartum and warrant proactive assessment within routine postpartum and gynecologic follow-up, with multidisciplinary management and referral for pelvic floor rehabilitation or urogynecologic evaluation when indicated.

items.title: Optimizing IUI: evidence-based guidance for use of add-ons and variations in IUI treatment, a British Fertility Society policy and practice guideline.
items.key: A systematic literature search identified 154 randomised controlled trials involving 34,825 participants. Meta-analyses were conducted where feasible. However, the limited availability of adequately powered trials and the predominantly low-quality evidence restrict the certainty of most recommendations. These limitations should be clearly communicated during patient counselling. Future research should prioritise high-quality trials evaluating the effectiveness of IUI add-ons in specific patient populations, considering underlying infertility diagnoses.

items.title: First trimester cervical length and cervical change in the prediction of prematurity related outcomes.
items.key:
RESULTS: First-trimester CL was significantly associated with late miscarriage (p=0.049), SPD 37 (p<0.014), cervical shortening (p<0.01), cerclage placement (p<0.01), and CAO (p<0.01). The risk increased nonlinearly, with a marked rise below 30 mm. For each 1 mm of decrease in first-trimester CL, the risk of CAO increased by 26%. Overall, mean CL change between first and second trimesters was minimal (-1.7%); however, pregnant individuals with CAO exhibited a significantly…
CONCLUSIONS: Shorter first-trimester CL and pronounced cervical shortening between the first and second trimester are significantly associated with a spectrum of the adverse pregnancy outcomes related to prematurity.

items.title: Endometrial fertility. Management of adenomyosis in gynecology and infertility.
items.key: IVF may overcome some adverse effects of adenomyosis on fertility, but its impact on embryo implantation remains problematic. Accordingly, available evidence suggests a possible reduction in live birth rates following IVF. However, current studies are limited by potential confounders. Studies investigating the use of medical pretreatment before IVF, including GnRH agonists, dienogest, or levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine systems, remain insufficient and inconsistent. Further prospective studies and randomized controlled trials using standardized inclusion criteria are needed.

items.title: Relugolix combination therapy for symptomatic uterine fibroids in routine practice: a multicentre, retrospective observational study of one-year outcomes.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 189 women were enrolled (mean age 44.4 years). Heavy menstrual bleeding was the main symptom (58.8 %). Amenorrhoea was achieved by 49.4 % of women (mean 64 days), and 70 % of the remainder reported improved bleeding. Haemoglobin rose from 10.5 g/dL at baseline to 11.8…
CONCLUSIONS: In routine European practice, relugolix combination therapy produced rapid control of heavy menstrual bleeding and a sustained rise in haemoglobin, though without significant change in fibroid or uterine volume. Counselling about expected early bleeding may improve adherence. These real-world data complement the LIBERTY trials and support use in daily practice, including as a bridge to surgery.

items.title: Association of intrinsic capacity with prevalent and incident cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic multimorbidity among Chinese adults aged 45 years or more: Evidence from a longitudinal cohort study.
items.key:
RESULTS: Each 1-point higher score for intrinsic capacity was associated with lower odds of prevalent multimorbidity (odds ratio 0.759, 95% confidence interval 0.713-0.807) and a lower risk of incident multimorbidity (hazard ratio 0.849, 95% confidence interval 0.805-0.896). Decreased intrinsic capacity was associated with higher odds of prevalent multimorbidity (odds ratio 1.649, 95% confidence interval 1.399-1.943) and a higher risk of incident…
CONCLUSIONS: Lower intrinsic capacity was associated with both prevalent and incident cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic multimorbidity. Intrinsic capacity assessment may complement disease-based health evaluation in middle-aged and older adults.

items.title: GESS-AEEM consensus on testosterone therapy in women: a clinical implementation framework.
items.key:
RESULTS: Physiological-dose transdermal testosterone may be considered for postmenopausal women with hypoactive sexual desire disorder after comprehensive biopsychosocial assessment. Serum testosterone should not be used diagnostically but supports safe prescribing and detection of supraphysiological exposure. The consensus addresses off-label prescribing, assay continuity, monitoring, discontinuation, safety communication and special populations. Non-transdermal formulations,…
CONCLUSIONS: This article does not propose a new therapeutic indication or supersede existing guidance. The article provides a contextualized implementation framework to support consistent and safe clinical practice.

items.title: The Obstetrician-Gynecologist's Role in Adoption.
items.key: Obstetrician-gynecologists may find themselves at the center of adoption discussions when caring for pregnant patients who are considering relinquishing their parental rights and placing their child for adoption. In this Committee Statement, the Committee on Ethics of the American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists discusses related ethical issues and aims to provide professional recommendations and physician safeguards while centering the patient with a trauma-informed approach.

items.title: Ovarian cancer screening using serum CA125 and transvaginal ultrasound: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Four randomised controlled trials were included in this meta-analysis, comprising 188147 participants in the screening group and 187394 in the control group. Pooled results showed no statistically significant difference in overall ovarian cancer incidence and ovarian…
CONCLUSION: For asymptomatic women in the general population, combined serum cancer antigen 125 and transvaginal ultrasound screening should be approached with caution. Current evidence indicates that this screening strategy neither reduced​ the overall incidence of ovarian cancer nor improved​ overall survival, despite potentially increasing the detection rate of Stage I and early-stage serous carcinoma.

items.title: The genetic path for cardiomyopathies after the European Society of Cardiology Guidelines 2023: a consensus statement of the Italian CardioGenetics Group.

items.title: Trends in Menopause Hormone Therapy.
Prevalence and impact of urinary incontinence in Canada: a systematic review of the quantitative and qualitative literature and a meta-analysis of quantitative data.
items.key: Out of 1089 titles, 34 were included: 16 prevalence, 10 impact, and 8 addressing both the prevalence and impact. UI was more prevalent in women than men (meta-analysis: 34% [95% CI, 25%-44%] vs 19% [95% CI, 7%-31%]; P < .001). Women were reluctant to seek medical help and suffered symptoms longer than men. Overall, the prevalence increased with age, reaching as high as 52% among women 85+ years. UI affected individuals socially, emotionally, physically, and financially. Included papers did not consider differences in prevalence or impact across ethnic, cultural, or socioeconomic groups. Increased awareness of management and treatment will improve quality of life.

items.title: Association of uterine-entry technique with chorioamniotic membrane separation after fetoscopic laser surgery for twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome: two-center retrospective cohort study.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Sharp-trocar entry during FLP for TTTS was associated with a lower incidence of CAS, longer latency from procedure to delivery and later gestational age at delivery compared with the Seldinger technique. Because the entry technique was center-specific, these differences cannot be attributed exclusively to the technique. Survival was similar between the two groups. Prospective studies in which both entry techniques are used in the same center are needed to confirm these findings. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

items.title: Impact of the pink October campaign on breast cancer screening in the Alpes-Maritimes region (France): A regional perspective.
items.key:
RESULTS: Organized screening activity peaked in October in each study year, with reported increases of 31% in 2022, 27% in 2023, and 48% in 2024 relative to the respective annual monthly means. The October-November comparison yielded P-values of…
CONCLUSION: Mammography activity, particularly organized screening, increased during the Pink October period in the Alpes-Maritimes region. However, the aggregated data cannot establish whether this increase represented additional screening or a redistribution of examinations across the calendar year. Further multicenter studies using longer time series and individual-level data are needed to assess the campaign's effect on screening participation.

CONCLUSION: PMOS patients have enhanced ABSI and BRI levels compared to women without the syndrome. Further high-quality studies from other world regions are needed to evaluate heterogeneity at different PMOS clinical stages.

items.title: Feasibility and factors associated with successful back transfer after maternal transfer for postpartum hemorrhage: A retrospective cohort study.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 163 eligible women, 92 (56.4%) underwent successful back transfer. A higher shock index at admission was negatively associated with successful back transfer (odds ratio, OR = 0.12; 95% confidence interval, 95% CI = 0.02-0.46; P = 0.005). Compared with tone, trauma (OR = 0.10, 95% CI = 0.03-0.28, P < 0.001)…
CONCLUSION: More than half of the women in this selected cohort underwent back transfer after maternal transfer for PPH. Lower shock index at admission, hemorrhage caused by uterine atony, and higher post-treatment hemoglobin concentration were associated with back transfer. These exploratory findings may inform future efforts to develop standardized back transfer criteria.

items.title: The effects of different types of hormonal contraception on bone mineral density in women of reproductive age: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Seven studies (k = 15 comparisons; n = 1,488 completers) met all inclusion criteria. The pooled WMD for lumbar spine BMD at 12 months was - 0.003 g/cm² (95% CI: -0.010 to + 0.005; p = 0.470; I² = 38.7%), below DXA precision limits and representing…
CONCLUSIONS: COCs do not materially alter BMD over 12 months in reproductive-age women, with consistent null effects across all progestin classes. A biologically plausible EE dose gradient was identified; DMPA use warrants individualized counselling given clinically relevant, though reversible, bone loss. Adequately powered long-term randomized trials targeting low-dose formulations, adolescents, and DMPA continuers are urgently needed.

items.title: Risk factors of cervical cancer among women in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis (2000-2025).
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Cervical cancer among women in Ethiopia is consistently associated with sexual behavior, infectious comorbidities, and reproductive factors. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening integrated prevention strategies, including expanding HPV vaccination coverage, improving access to cervical cancer screening, and enhancing integration with HIV care services. Addressing modifiable associated factors may help reduce the burden of cervical cancer in Ethiopia.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of the Oral Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone Antagonist DW4902 for Heavy Menstrual Bleeding in Uterine Fibroids: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Phase II Trial.

Amenorrhea rates were likewise significantly higher in the DW4902 groups (≥ 73.33%), with bleeding suppression evident from Weeks 2 to 6. Haemoglobin levels increased significantly in the 160 and 240 mg groups. Fibroid and uterine volumes and fibroid-related pain were significantly reduced across all DW4902 dose groups. Hormone levels recovered after treatment discontinuation,…
CONCLUSIONS: DW4902 demonstrated a robust efficacy in reducing menstrual bleeding and improving fibroid-related outcomes with an acceptable short-term safety and bone density profile.

items.title: Management of Infants Born to Mothers with Q Fever During Pregnancy.
items.key: There were no cases of transmission through breastmilk. Infection-control precautions ranged from standard to airborne. Evidence indicated that vertical transmission to the fetus or live-born infant is rare. Maternal illness and fetal loss appear related to placental infection. Separation of mother and infant or avoidance of breastfeeding are not supported. Management should prioritize placental handling precautions and structured infant follow-up. No published clinical consensus guidelines exist for management of infants born to mothers with Q fever (Coxiella burnetii) during pregnancy. Global collaboration and evidence gathering can inform evidence-based guidelines.

items.title: Routine Prenatal Ultrasound at 36 Weeks: Impact on Obstetric Clinical Outcomes.
items.key:
RESULTS: SGA infants delivered at 37-38 weeks' gestation increased from 18.7% to 38.1% post intervention (p = 0.04) with a concomitant overall reduction in NICU admissions (OR = 0.74, 95% CI: 0.66-0.82). The prenatal detection rate of breech presentation increased significantly from 78% to almost…
CONCLUSIONS: Routine 36-week scan embedded within a structured clinical management pathway was associated with significant changes in obstetric metrics and improved pregnancy outcome. Overall, these findings provide real-world evidence on how a universal third-trimester ultrasound may selectively influence obstetric management and inform the ongoing debate on routine prenatal screening strategies.

items.title: Phenotypic Severity Determines Overall Pregnancy Outcome and Survival in Fetuses With Turner Syndrome: Insights From a Large Multicenter Cohort.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 726 pregnancies, 451 (62.1%) were ET, 275 (37.9%) continued; of these, 98 (35.6%) resulted in LB and 177 (64.4%) in SID. Severe phenotypes were present in 92.4% of terminations, 81.0% of SIDs and 33.0% of LB. Mosaic and structural karyotypes showed a lower risk of intrauterine death than 45,X (HR 0.28 and 0.32), while severe phenotype strongly predicted mortality (HR 4.82). Most SIDs occurred before 30 weeks' gestation (median 21 weeks). MS was 9.6% for 45,X, 50.0% for mosaic and 36.8% for structural variants.
CONCLUSION: Survival in prenatally diagnosed TS is higher than historically reported. Phenotypic severity is the principal determinant of outcome.

items.title: Injectable Hyaluronic Acid for Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Injectable hyaluronic acid-based therapies are emerging non-hormonal interventions for vulvovaginal symptoms associated with GSM. Current evidence does not yet establish their role as routine or guideline-recommended treatments. This evidentiary position should be considered separately from the intended purpose and regulatory status of individual devices. Larger independent trials, longer-term safety data, and health-economic evaluations are needed to define their comparative clinical role.

items.title: Age and sex related differences on genotype stratified CYP450 mediated metabolism rate in healthy populations; a systematic review.
items.key: One study suggested a decrease in CYP3A activity with age. Limited evidence from two studies suggested lower CYP2C9 activity in females. For CYP2C19, results were mixed, but oral contraceptive use reduced activity and age-related decline was reported. Limited adult evidence suggested lower CYP2D6 activity in females within genotype groups. In infants, CYP2D6 activity was detectable early and remained relatively stable throughout the first year of life. Overall, sex- and age-related differences in CYP activity appear enzyme- and context-specific, but the heterogeneous evidence does not support sex- or age-based dose adjustment.

items.title: ART and post-partum haemorrhage: real-world cohort study, mediation and causal forest analysis from 259,135 deliveries.
items.key:
RESULTS: PPH incidence was significantly higher in the ART group versus controls (3.0% [590/19,788] versus 1.4% [3254/239,347], P < 0.001). After adjustments for baseline- and delivery-related covariates, ART was significantly associated with increased PPH risk (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] = 2.02, 95% confidence interval [95% CI] 1.83-2.24, P < 0.001). Adjusted sensitivity analysis showed a 14-15 ml increase in 2 h post-partum blood loss in ART patients…
CONCLUSIONS: ART conception is associated with elevated PPH risk, with multiple pregnancy, placenta praevia and placental abruption as important mediators. Clinical attention to PPH risk assessment in ART pregnancies should be strengthened.

items.title: Day-5 or day-6 sequential hatching and biopsy versus day-3 hatching before blastocyst biopsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: No significant differences were observed in ongoing pregnancy or miscarriage rates. Day-5 or day-6 sequential hatching and biopsy, however, was associated with increased mosaicism (two RCTs, pooled OR 2.50, 95% CI 1.97 to 3.17, P < 0.001) and no-PGT-result reporting (two RCTs, pooled OR 5.84, 95% CI 3.09 to 11.01, P < 0.001), despite comparable euploidy and aneuploidy rates. Our findings suggest day-5 or day-6 sequential hatching and biopsy may be associated with improved embryo transfer outcomes compared with day-3 artificial hatching, whereas the increased reporting of mosaicism and no-PGT-result may have limited clinical implications given their low absolute incidence.

CONCLUSION: Immersive VR during eTVS was associated with reduced anxiety and stable pain scores. These findings warrant further evaluation in an adequately powered randomized trial.

CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, UI patients following repeated IUI failures demonstrated neither markedly superior nor inferior cLBRs compared to the control population. CONCLUSIONS: Despite a high prevalence of recognised PFD risk factors, 38.7% of women reported no antenatal PFD symptom enquiry, and only 19.4% received practical PFME instruction. These findings highlight opportunities to improve the consistency of antenatal pelvic floor care through routine symptom enquiry, preventative education and targeted specialist support, in accordance with national recommendations.

items.title: Gitelman syndrome complicated by pregnancy: clinical management and maternal-fetal outcomes - a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fifty-six studies (96 pregnancies, 81 women) from 19 countries were included. Among pregnancies with available outcome data, reported maternal complications included gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) (11.5%), oligohydramnios (9.4%), and preeclampsia/hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets…
CONCLUSIONS: Preconception counseling and multidisciplinary care with close electrolyte monitoring and individualized supplementation may benefit GS-complicated pregnancies, but evidence is limited by case-report data, publication bias, and heterogeneity. Larger prospective studies with standardized outcome reporting are needed to clarify risk factors and guide clinical management.

items.title: Five-year risk of cardiovascular events in women with history of pregnancy complicated by fetal growth restriction.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: FGR in a first pregnancy is associated with increased maternal composite cardiovascular risk, including heart failure, acute myocardial infarction and cerebral infarction/ischemic stroke, within 5 years postpartum. These findings suggest that FGR may be a marker of early cardiovascular vulnerability. However, residual confounding, particularly by unmeasured timing or severity of pre-eclampsia, cannot be excluded. Also, FGR was identified using coding constructs based on electronic health records, which may include overlap with broader 'suspected poor growth' phenotypes such as small-for-gestational age, hence potentially diluting the observed associations. Earlier risk assessment and preventive strategies may help to reduce the risk of long-term morbidity and mortality in this population. © 2026 The Author(s). items.title: Multidisciplinary care models for managing pregnancies complicated with chronic diseases: A systematic review.
items.key: Reduced maternal and fetal morbidity was also reported. Clinicians and policymakers can use this collective description to select strategies for effective multidisciplinary care models appropriate for the socio-economic, health system, and disease-related context of their specific setting. Studies with robust methodology would provide stronger evidence supporting multidisciplinary care during pregnancy. Standardized reporting of multidisciplinary care provision is also important for deriving sound conclusions about the effectiveness of the models and their adaptability across different health systems.

items.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
items.key: Postnatal drought exposure was consistently associated with acute and chronic malnutrition and increased mortality risk, whereas evidence for infectious diseases and micronutrient deficiencies was more heterogeneous across studies. Across studies, the magnitude of these effects varied according to drought severity, socioeconomic conditions, and access to health services. Overall, the evidence suggests that drought exposure from pregnancy through early childhood is associated with multiple adverse health outcomes. Strengthening social protection, food security, and health interventions in drought-prone settings may help reduce the burden of these impacts on child health.

items.title: Associations between cesarean delivery and adverse maternal and newborn outcomes by Robson Group: An analysis of the PRISMA study cohort in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 10 996 women, 29% delivered by CS. Group 5 (prior CS) and group 10 (preterm) were the largest contributors, accounting for 28% and 17% of all CS deliveries, respectively. Between-site differences in CS incidence were most pronounced for groups 2 and…
CONCLUSION: Repeat CS, preterm deliveries, labor induction, and pre-labor CS were drivers of CS. Although differences in risk magnitude associated with CS across Robson groups revealed important patterns for quality improvement, these estimates should not be interpreted as causal effects. Equipping facilities to manage labor induction, trials of labor after cesarean, and preterm deliveries is critical to improving quality of care.

items.title: Quality-of-life trajectories after laparoscopic surgery for endometriosis across public and private healthcare pathways: A prospective longitudinal study.
items.key: CONCLUSION: QoL improved across most domains during the 6 months after laparoscopic endometriosis surgery in both public and private healthcare pathways and across endometriosis phenotypes. Differences in longitudinal trajectories between healthcare pathways were identified in selected SF-36 domains, whereas disease-specific EHP-30 trajectories were broadly similar between groups. Infertility-related QoL concerns did not significantly change during follow-up. These findings indicate that postoperative QoL trajectories may vary across specific health domains and healthcare pathways but remain broadly similar across endometriosis phenotypes.

items.title: Revealing Neuroplasticity Following Sacral Neuromodulation Treatment with Functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy.

The SNM cohort was compared with healthy controls (n = 9) and an OAB cohort (without SNM; n = 11). The SNM O2Hb pattern was most similar to that in normal participants, though with a smaller increase in magnitude. Non-SNM-treated OAB O2Hb patterns were stable or decreasing.
CONCLUSIONS: The findings contribute to supporting the hypothesis that the PFC plays an inhibitory role in voiding function, which can be improved in women after SNM treatment.

The composite surgical complication outcome occurred in 4.5% of patients overall and occurred for fewer patients having robotic approach (4.3% vs 5.3%, P = 0.04). CONCLUSIONS: Robotic MISCP may be associated with slightly fewer 30-day complications than laparoscopic MISCP although overall complication rates are low.

items.title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding access to sexual and reproductive health and gender-based violence services in Brazil since the SARS-CoV-2 pandemic: A multi-stakeholder qualitative analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 99 participants contributed to 120 interviews. Political-institutional mistrust, conflicting public messaging, and health system reorganization affected access to SRH and GBV services. Although healthcare professionals reported continuity of essential services, women described reduced availability of gynecological care and contraceptive services. Socioeconomic barriers, transportation difficulties, and poor coordination further limited…
CONCLUSION: The impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on SRH and GBV service access in Brazil was not solely due to service disruption but resulted from dynamic interactions across political, institutional, interpersonal, and temporal levels.

items.title: Non-hormonal management of menopause symptoms-the statement of the European Society of Gynecology.
items.key:
RESULTS: Lifestyle modification, including healthy diet, regular physical activity, weight control, sleep hygiene, and behavioral interventions, forms the foundation of menopausal care. Among…
CONCLUSIONS: Non-hormonal therapies provide effective and individualized treatment options for menopausal symptoms, particularly for women who are unable or unwilling to use MHT. Neurokinin receptor antagonists, selected pharmacologic agents, psychological interventions, and targeted GSM therapies represent the strongest evidence-based approaches currently available. The choice of treatment should consider symptom profile, contraindications, adverse effects, regulatory approval, and patient preferences.

items.title: Controversies in NEN: An ENETS position statement on fertility, sexual function and pregnancy in patients with neuroendocrine neoplasms.
items.key: Pregnancy in patients with NENs is feasible in selected cases but requires careful planning and close monitoring due to potential risks related to tumour behaviour and treatment exposure. The available evidence is limited and largely based on small series, highlighting the need for individualised decision-making. This statement emphasises the importance of integrating reproductive counselling into routine care, and promoting collaboration among NEN physicians, reproductive specialists, and other healthcare professionals to improve patient-centred outcomes.

items.title: Patient Perceptions of Clinician Attire in the Outpatient Urogynecology Clinic.

Formal attire with a white coat received the highest ratings for professionalism and aptitude, whereas scrubs scored highest for friendliness and empathy. Mixed-effects models…
CONCLUSIONS: Clinician attire significantly shapes patient perceptions in urogynecology. Although white coats bolster perceived professionalism and aptitude, scrubs enhance friendliness and empathy. Attire is a modifiable factor that clinicians can strategically align with the goals of specific encounters.

items.title: The effectiveness of health information systems in supporting early detection and referral pathways for high-risk pregnancies: A systematic review.
items.key: However, the evidence base was limited by heterogeneous study designs, limited direct mortality outcomes, infrastructure constraints, digital literacy gaps, and interoperability challenges. Direct evidence demonstrating reductions in maternal mortality remains limited. HIS can strengthen maternal surveillance, referral pathways, and clinical decision support for high-risk pregnancies. Sustainable impact requires integrated infrastructure, workforce training, effective data governance, and standardized outcome evaluation.

items.title: Effectiveness of mobile applications in pregnancy care: An umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.

Future research should focus on high-quality, large-scale, long-term trials with culturally sensitive, personalized approaches. Strong collaboration among researchers, healthcare providers, and technology developers is essential to fully harness the impact of mobile applications on maternal and neonatal health.

items.title: 2025 Harriet Dustan Lecture: Sex Differences in Immune-Mediated Hypertension: Why Menopause Matters.
items.key: Despite these sex differences, sex-specific clinical practice guidelines are still sparse, as is the consideration of a woman's hormonal status. In addition, preclinical models of immune-mediated hypertension are still mainly performed in male animals. The goal of this review is to highlight recent advancements in the field of sex differences in immune-mediated hypertension and to identify the major gaps in understanding immune mechanisms that lead to hypertension development in males and females, and as menopause progresses.

items.title: Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.

In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy…
CONCLUSIONS: Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

items.title: Weight-loss effects of GLP-1 receptor agonists in reproductive-age women with overweight or obesity and polycystic ovary syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

CONCLUSIONS: In reproductive-aged women with overweight or obesity and PCOS, GLP-1 receptor agonists may offer weight-loss benefits and improvements in central obesity compared with conventional regimens; however, these findings are derived from a small, clinically heterogeneous pool of trials with short follow-up and low-certainty evidence. The pooled estimates should therefore be interpreted with caution and considered hypothesis-generating rather than definitive.

items.title: Is It Safe to Treat Patients with Botulinum Toxin A During the Peri-Conception Period of Pregnancy? A Systematic Review of the Literature.

One case of preterm labor with fetal renal anomaly and one case of fetal growth restriction were reported.
CONCLUSION: Peri-conception botulinum toxin exposure was not associated with increased adverse outcomes compared with population rates, though evidence is limited by small, heterogenous studies.

items.title: Comparative Effects of Technology-Based Educational Interventions for Improving Cancer Screening Among Migrant Women: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fifteen studies (16 datasets) were included. Multicomponent interventions significantly increased screening uptake compared with usual care (odds ratio 5.50, 95% confidence interval 2.56-11.82) and ranked as the most effective strategy (P score = 0.92). Text messaging, voice messaging, and video-based interventions demonstrated positive but nonsignificant effects.
CONCLUSIONS: Multicomponent technology-based educational interventions were more effective than single-modality approaches in improving cancer screening uptake among migrant women.

items.title: Concomitant Right-Sided Bowel Resection at the Time of Left Colorectal Surgery for Deep Endometriosis: Is It Associated With Increased Major Morbidity? Evidence From 1,058 Patients.

These findings support individualized risk counseling and should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of events in some subgroups.

Routine assessment, careful medication review, and appropriate deprescribing may reduce avoidable harm. Integrating burden assessment into prescribing systems and clinical decision-support tools may further promote safer pharmacotherapy in an ageing society.

items.title: The endometrial microbiome and reproductive outcomes following assisted reproductive technologies: A systematic review.

items.title: The Rising Tide of Cardiovascular Risk in Younger Women.
items.key: Many women today will arrive at menopause with more advanced CVD risk than what was encountered in the past. If women are considering HT for menopausal symptom relief or bone preservation, careful consideration is required to identify and treat modifiable CVD risks-dyslipidemia, glucose intolerance, hypertension, and, increasingly, obesity-to targets established by guidelines before initiating HT. Risk assessment with validated risk calculators can help stratify CVD risk, a factor that determines lipid lowering therapy, and the advisability and choice of menopausal HT. The rising tide of cardiovascular risk does not have to make waves at menopause.

items.title: Efficacy of dietary supplements in improving sperm parameters in men with infertility: a network meta-analysis.
items.key: For improving total sperm motility, the top five supplements were omega-3, curcumin nanomicelle, LAC, zinc, and ALA. Appropriate dietary supplements demonstrate significant efficacy in improving semen parameters in male patients with infertility. However, their efficacy varies across semen parameters. Zinc and omega-3 ranked relatively high across all six semen parameters. In clinical practice, the individual characteristics of different patients should be considered when selecting therapeutic agents and formulating personalized dietary supplement regimens.

items.title: Updated clinical recommendations for cardiovascular risk assessment to facilitate hormone therapy prescribing: incorporating PREVENT risk calculator and the 2026 multisociety lipid guidelines.
items.key: This perspective provides a practical framework for integrating PREVENT-derived risk categories into menopause care. We outline cardiovascular risk stratification strategies for women considering HT, discuss the role of coronary artery calcium scoring and female-specific risk enhancers, and align contemporary lipid management recommendations with decisions regarding initiation of HT, including route of administration. By integrating cardiovascular risk assessment and menopause management, clinicians can optimize cardiovascular risk reduction and individualize treatment decisions for symptomatic midlife women.

Associations did not meet the false discovery rate threshold for diabetes (PR: 1.26; 95% CI: 0.94-1.71), hypertension (PR: 1.07; 95% CI: 0.93-1.22), osteoporosis (PR: 1.20; 95% CI: 0.90-1.60),…
CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral oophorectomy after natural menopause was associated with higher self-reported cardiovascular disease prevalence. Because outcome timing relative to surgery was unavailable and residual confounding remains, this cross-sectional association should not be interpreted as causal or as a basis for clinical recommendations.

items.title: Phenotypic age acceleration mediates the association between plant-based diet and advanced cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome among postmenopausal women: a population-based cross-sectional analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among the study population, 658 participants (22.0%) were identified with advanced CKM. A one-unit increase in the plant-based diet index (PDI) and the healthful PDI was associated with a lower odds of advanced CKM (adjusted odds ratio [OR]: 0.98; 95% CI: 0.96-1.00 and OR: 0.97; 95% CI: 0.94-0.99, respectively). In contrast, each one-unit increase in the unhealthful PDI was associated with 4% higher odds of advanced CKM…
CONCLUSIONS: Higher adherence to healthy plant-based dietary patterns is associated with a lower likelihood of advanced CKM among postmenopausal women. The association between PDI with advanced CKM may be partly mediated through reduced phenotypic age acceleration.

items.title: Breast cancer in premenopausal and postmenopausal women: clinicopathological findings and survival outcomes from a large registry-based cohort in Southern Iran.
items.key:
RESULTS: Premenopausal women more frequently presented with aggressive tumor features, including larger tumor size, multifocality, necrosis, and adverse pathologic characteristics (all P<0.01). Postmenopausal patients had a higher prevalence of estrogen receptor-positive tumors (P=0.003)…
CONCLUSIONS: Menopausal status was associated with distinct tumor biology, clinicopathological features, and treatment patterns in breast cancer, with premenopausal patients showing more aggressive disease. Although menopausal status showed some association with survival outcomes, its effect appeared largely driven by age and underlying tumor characteristics, suggesting limited independent prognostic value.

items.title: The relationships among gender perceptions, internalized misogyny, and body shame in postmenopausal women: a structural equation modeling study.
items.key:
RESULTS: Gender perception was negatively correlated with internalized misogyny (r=-0.478, P<0.001) and body shame (r=-0.286, P<0.001), whereas internalized misogyny was positively correlated with body shame (r=0.320, P<0.001). In the structural model, more egalitarian gender perception was associated with lower…
CONCLUSIONS: More egalitarian gender perception was associated with lower internalized misogyny and body shame, whereas greater internalized misogyny was associated with greater body shame. Given the cross-sectional design, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of temporal or causal relationships. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify these relationships.

In the menopause phase, FM and FFM showed clinically significant associations with total mortality (FM 1.18 [1.02-1.38]; FFM 0.71 [0.50-1.00]). These associations were not…
CONCLUSION: Higher FM is associated with a higher risk of MACE/total mortality, whereas higher FFM is associated with a lower risk of total mortality. Associations noted in women in the menopause phase but not among similarly aged women suggest ovarian aging may influence these relationships.

items.title: Dry eye disease in the menopausal transition: toward recognition as a hormonal manifestation.
items.key: e significantly worse in postmenopausal compared with premenopausal women even when subjective symptoms are similar, mirroring the symptom-sign dissociation well recognized in genitourinary syndrome of menopause. This hormonally mediated dry eye is described in recent literature as menopausal dry eye. This opinion advocates for routine screening using the validated Ocular Surface Disease Index-6 questionnaire, counseling patients on the ocular implications of hormone therapy and timely referral to eye care providers for persistent or moderate-to-severe symptoms. Recognizing dry eye as a menopausal disease can improve how ocular symptoms are attributed, discussed and treated in midlife women.

items.title: A Systematic Review on the Impact of Mental Health on Reproductive Hormones and Fertility Outcomes.
items.key: Psychological interventions showed more consistent benefits for reducing distress and improving coping than for improving reproductive endpoints. Psychological stress and reproductive health appear to be interrelated; however, the available evidence does not establish a definitive causal relationship between stress and impaired fertility. Interpretation is limited by heterogeneity in study designs, populations, stress measures, and reproductive outcomes, as well as overlapping evidence bases and the predominance of secondary literature. Prospective primary studies using standardized measures and rigorously…

There were two randomised controlled trials, one single-arm open-label interventional study, eleven cohort studies, and nine case series. Five studies investigated hormonal treatments, one other study assessed other pharmacological treatments, sixteen…
SUMMARY ANSWER: The use of hormonal therapies and surgery was associated with improvements in pain symptoms in most studies; however, the certainty of evidence was very low, meaning that the true impact of these treatments remains uncertain.

items.title: Prevalence of Pathogenic Variants and Variants of Uncertain Significance in Patients With Epithelial Ovarian Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: BRCA1, BRCA2, RAD51D, and RAD51C exhibited the greatest disparities in the proportions of PV and VUS, indicating a positive risk-benefit balance regarding clinical decision-making. Our findings suggest that the probability of detecting a VUS in other panel genes is significantly higher than in classic DDR genes, highlighting the underreporting of VUS in clinical studies. Routine clinical reporting may prioritize well-established EOC-risk genes, with multigene panel testing reserved for selected subgroups. Improving the reporting and classification of VUS is essential, and future studies should prioritize gene-specific VUS evaluation.

items.title: Artificial intelligence-based models for predicting bronchopulmonary dysplasia in preterm infants: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Eighteen studies were included. Random Forest and XGBoost were the most frequently used algorithms. AUC values for the best-performing models ranged from 0.80 to 1.00, showing improved performance as postnatal variables were incorporated. However, the PROBAST assessment revealed a high overall risk of bias in 72.2% of the studies, primarily due to deficiencies in…
CONCLUSIONS: AI-based models show high discriminative capacity for BPD prediction; however, they have not yet demonstrated clear superiority over conventional statistical models in robust comparisons. Their routine clinical implementation is currently limited by poor methodological quality and scarce external validation.

items.title: Comparative efficacy and safety of nonhormonal prescription drugs for vasomotor symptoms in women with breast cancer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

RESULTS: Eighteen publications, corresponding to 19 study/substudy records and 2,224 randomized or allocated participants, were included. Five interventions were significantly more effective than placebo: escitalopram (SMD -1.08, 95% CI -1.80 to -0.37), desvenlafaxine 50 mg (SMD -0.87, 95% CI -1.60 to -0.15), desvenlafaxine 100 mg (SMD -0.80, 95% CI -1.44 to -0.15), elinzanetant (SMD -0.51, 95% CI -0.95 to -0.07), and venlafaxine 75 mg (SMD -0.42, 95% CI -0.76 to…
CONCLUSION: Nonhormonal prescription drugs are not interchangeable for breast cancer-related VMS. Elinzanetant provides the strongest high-certainty evidence among newer targeted options, and venlafaxine 75 mg is the best-supported…

items.title: The strategic integration of emergency obstetric and neonatal care with contraceptive services.
items.key: the postpartum period after an obstetric emergency represents a critical, frequently missed opportunity for contraceptive counseling, particularly in low-resource and humanitarian settings where subsequent access to care is uncertain. We propose practical strategies for integration at the facility, health system, and global levels, including standardized counseling prompts, aligned supply chains, updated training curricula, and incorporation of contraceptive indicators into EmONC guidance and monitoring tools. Embedding contraception within EmONC would strengthen continuity across the maternal health continuum and better align global frameworks with the clinical realities of obstetric risk.

items.title: Investigating the association between blood lipid profiles and insulin resistance and β-cell function indices in pregnant women.
items.key:
RESULTS: After adjustment for age and early-pregnancy body mass index, all seven lipid markers were significantly associated with continuous HOMA-IR and the Matsuda index (all nominal P < 0.05). No statistically significant associations…
CONCLUSION: First-trimester lipid markers were associated with second-trimester IR and insulin-sensitivity indices, whereas no statistically significant associations were observed with the surrogate BCF indices used in this study. Triglycerides/high-density lipoprotein cholesterol showed moderate apparent discrimination for cohort-defined low insulin sensitivity and should be considered a hypothesis-generating candidate marker requiring external validation.

items.title: Clustering of Maternal and Perinatal Complications Following Fresh and Frozen Embryo Transfer in First-Time Mothers: A Population-Based Cohort Study.
items.key:
RESULTS: In first-time mothers, three of every four singleton pregnancies after frozen-ET and fresh-ET were without maternal and perinatal complications, compared to four of every five pregnancies…
CONCLUSION: In this study, we observed that most first-time mothers experienced pregnancies without maternal and perinatal complications following ART, and when complications occurred, they were typically without additional complications. Although single and multiple complications were more common following ART than after NC, the absolute differences were small. These findings may help set realistic expectations when counselling people who consider ART treatment, or those already in treatment.

items.title: Pre-eclampsia screening and prevention: Implementing FIGO guidelines in a Thai population.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 1713 pregnancies, 71 developed pre-eclampsia (4.1%), including 49 with severe features. Overall, 1106 women were screened (64.6%), but coverage reached 93.6% by the end of implementation. The screen-positive rate was 11.3%. Detection rates were 61.7% for overall pre-eclampsia, 69.6% for delivery before 37 weeks of gestation, 87.5% for delivery before 34 weeks of gestation, and 100% for delivery…
CONCLUSION: FIGO-based first-trimester screening was feasible in routine care, with increasing coverage as implementation matured, near-universal aspirin uptake, and clinically useful detection of preterm pre-eclampsia. Aspirin use was not significantly associated with severe bleeding.

items.title: Association between polycystic ovary syndrome and asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: 13 studies (including over 28 million women, 11 cross-sectional and 2 longitudinal) were included. Of these, eight were assessed as moderate or high risk of bias. Meta-analyses showed that PCOS was associated with a higher odds of asthma in both crude (OR 1.59, 95% CI 1.44 to 1.76, I²=72.0%, τ²=0.009) and adjusted analyses (OR 1.57, 95% CI 1.40 to 1.77, I²=90.6%, τ²=0.007). The…
CONCLUSIONS: PCOS appeared to be associated with asthma but this was driven by findings from cross-sectional studies which are at risk of reverse causation. Lung function evidence remains inconclusive. Future studies should prioritise standardised methods and longitudinal designs to establish temporality.

items.title: Robotic-Assisted Uterus Transplantation: A Cadaveric Feasibility Model.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Robotic-assisted implantation of a uterine graft is technically feasible in a cadaveric model. This robotic approach may offer a minimally invasive approach to uterus transplantation; further preclinical and clinical studies are warranted.

items.title: State contraceptive coverage and interstate disparities in postabortion contraception receipt among patients traveling for care.
items.key:
RESULTS: Idaho residents were more likely to receive no contraception following abortion (43.5% Idaho vs 34.7% Oregon) and less likely to receive LARC (19.8% vs…
CONCLUSIONS: Oregon's income-based contraceptive coverage program was associated with a meaningful reduction in interstate disparities in receipt of postabortion contraception for patients traveling for procedural abortion care.
IMPLICATIONS: Income-based contraceptive coverage programs that extend to out-of-state patients may reduce geographic disparities in postabortion contraception receipt. As more people travel for needed abortion care, receiving states should expand access to postabortion contraception regardless of residency.

items.title: Evaluation of artificial intelligence-based blastocysts: effect on viability and metabolic function of shortened warming protocol and fatty acid supplementation.
items.key:
RESULTS: Overall post-warming survival was 98.5%. Artificial intelligence scores decreased after vitrification-warming but partially recovered after culture (P < 0.0001 for all), with no differences between groups. Necrosis was significantly higher in shortened-protocol groups (P ≤ 0.0166). Artificial…
CONCLUSIONS: The shortened warming protocol increased necrosis in poor-quality blastocysts, impaired mitochondrial activity and reduced outgrowth area in vitro. Fatty-acid supplementation supported mitochondrial recovery. Artificial intelligence-based scores reflected necrosis-associated impairment and may enable its non-invasive estimation. Larger studies are needed to validate these findings.

items.title: Ovarian function and fertility after childhood cancer: risk assessment in the era of novel treatments.
items.key: This review examines the effect of conventional cancer treatments on ovarian function and fertility, as well as the methods currently used to assess ovarian reserve in female childhood cancer survivors and preserve fertility. It also considers how evolving treatment strategies across major cancers affecting adolescents and young adults may influence reproductive outcomes. Particular attention is given to the limited evidence available on the reproductive effects of targeted treatments and immunotherapies. Further prospective studies integrating ovarian reserve markers with long-term reproductive outcomes are needed, particularly for newer anticancer treatments.

CONCLUSIONS: Combination therapy may improve selected short-term metabolic and androgen-related measures in women with PMOS and overweight or obesity. Genetic findings provide complementary evidence linking genetically proxied GLP1R expression to androgen-related traits. Larger, longer-term trials are needed to determine whether these changes translate into reproductive and patient-important benefits.

items.title: Prevalence of intimate partner violence against women in East Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 41 studies. The overall pooled prevalence of IPV was 42.8% (95% CI: 38.3-47.9%), indicating high heterogeneity (I2 = 99.6%). Subgroup analyses revealed significant variation: the highest prevalence was among contraceptive users (72.6%, based on a single study) and ever-married/partnered women (55.1%), while the lowest was…
CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis confirms a high prevalence of IPV among women in East Africa, with substantial variation across subpopulations, countries, and methodological factors. Findings highlight the need for targeted, context-specific interventions and the importance of standardized measurement tools in surveillance and research.

items.title: Comprehensive meta-analysis and meta-regression of peripartum cardiomyopathy: risk factors, cardiac function, and maternal-neonatal outcomes in 66,908 PPCM patients.
items.key: CONCLUSION: The high prevalence of NYHA class III/IV symptoms at diagnosis underscores the importance of early detection and monitoring, while the variation in reported use of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) across studies highlights potential opportunities to optimize treatment in patients with PPCM. The observed improvement in LVEF during follow-up indicates that cardiac recovery is possible in patients with PPCM. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously given the observational nature and substantial heterogeneity of the included studies.

items.title: Intracrinology and tissue-selective effects of tibolone: mechanisms and implications.
items.key:
RESULTS: Tibolone acts predominantly as a prodrug and is converted into three active metabolites: the estrogenic compounds 3α-hydroxytibolone and 3β-hydroxytibolone, and the Δ4-isomer, which has progestogenic and androgenic properties. Experimental evidence indicates that tissue-specific differences in enzyme expression, sulfation,…
CONCLUSION: Intracrinology provides a biologically plausible framework for understanding the tissue-selective effects of tibolone. However, clinical findings are largely compatible with, rather than confirmatory of, this mechanism, and the balance of benefits and risks appears to vary according to tissue, clinical context and individual patient characteristics.

items.title: Birth and long-term health outcomes of intrauterine offspring after local methotrexate treatment for heterotopic pregnancy: A retrospective study and focused literature review.

Matched comparative…
CONCLUSION: Most live-born offspring following local MTX treatment for HP had no congenital anomalies, and no long-term offspring outcome comparison remained statistically significant after FDR correction. However, congenital anomalies were reported in both our cohort and the published literature, and the small sample size and limited evidence preclude firm conclusions regarding long-term safety.

items.title: TMEFF2 is associated with trophoblast dysfunction in missed abortion.
items.key:
RESULTS: TMEFF2 expression was significantly higher in the chorionic villous tissue from women with MA than in tissue from controls. In HTR-8/SVneo cells, TMEFF2 overexpression was associated with reduced proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration, whereas TMEFF2 knockdown showed the opposite pattern.
CONCLUSION: TMEFF2 is upregulated in chorionic villous tissue from women with MA and is associated with reduced proliferation-related metabolic activity and migration in HTR-8/SVneo cells in vitro. These findings provide preliminary evidence of an association between TMEFF2 and MA.

items.title: Utility of Artificial Intelligence in Diagnosing Image-Based Vaginal Pathology.
items.key:
RESULTS: Experts achieved top 3 diagnostic accuracy of 84% and top 1 accuracy of 66%. AI systems demonstrated variable performance, with mean top 3 accuracy of 51.8% and a mean top 1 accuracy of 32.5%. ChatGPT and Gemini achieved the highest AI performance (68% and 68% top 3 accuracy; 44% and 52% top 1 accuracy, respectively). In malignant cases…
CONCLUSIONS: Publicly available AI models demonstrate moderate accuracy in identifying vaginal pathology from images but perform below expert clinicians. While some models approach expert performance in detecting malignancy, they tend to over-recommend urgent care, highlighting a limited but evolving role for patient-facing AI in image-based triage.

items.title: Efficacy of SGLT2 Inhibitors With or Without Metformin Compared With Metformin Alone in Women With Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.key:
RESULTS: Five trials (292 women) were included. SGLT2 inhibitors did not differ significantly from metformin in body weight (MD = -2.06 kg; 95% CI -5.79 to 1.68) or BMI (MD = -0.34 kg/m2; 95% CI -0.78 to 0.10), or most hormonal, glycemic and anthropometric outcomes. However, they significantly reduced triglycerides (MD = -0.21 mmol/L; 95% CI -0.38 to -0.05) and…
CONCLUSION: SGLT2 inhibitors, alone or with metformin, did not differ significantly from metformin across most metabolic and endocrine outcomes, with modest benefits on triglycerides and diastolic blood pressure. Metformin remains first-line therapy; SGLT2 inhibitors may be considered in selected patients pending larger trials.

items.title: Use of transvaginal and transabdominal cerclage in the Nordic countries: A survey of incidences and indications.
items.key:
RESULTS: The estimated incidence per 100 000 births of history-indicated transvaginal cerclage was 231 in DK, 70 in FI, 140 in IS, 133 in NO, and 166 in SE. For ultrasound-indicated transvaginal cerclage, the estimated incidence per 100 000 births was 166 in DK, 21 in FI, 140 in IS, 17 in NO, and 59 in SE. For transabdominal cerclage, the…
CONCLUSIONS: There is substantial variation in the use of cervical cerclage between the Nordic countries. We advocate for a harmonized Nordic model of cerclage care to ensure equitable and consistent practice across countries, coupled with a Nordic research collaboration network that can drive knowledge generation and implementation across the region.

items.title: Maternal - fetal outcomes and risk factors of uterine rupture in the setting of pregnant women with scarred versus unscarred uterus: a systematic review and meta - analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Compared to patients with scarred uterine rupture, unscarred uterine rupture is associated with significantly higher risks of perinatal mortality, hysterectomy, and postpartum hemorrhage. Additionally, advanced maternal age, a higher incidence of oxytocin, induction of labor, and malpresentation were associated with rupture in the unscarred uterus group. These factors should be taken seriously. Early identification of relevant risk factors is crucial to avoid potential obstetric emergencies, prevent diagnostic delays, and allow timely surgical intervention to improve maternal and neonatal outcomes.

items.title: KRAS and endometriosis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: Variant allele fractions were consistently low (<20%), reflecting clonal epithelial expansion. KRAS-positive patients demonstrated greater disease extent and surgical complexity, though associations with pain, infertility, and recurrence were not statistically significant.ConclusionPreliminary evidence suggests that KRAS mutations are common in endometriosis; however, findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to substantial study heterogeneity and limited available data. KRAS may hold biological significance as a biomarker; however, current evidence is insufficient to support routine clinical use.

items.title: The challenge of Adenomyosis across the ART journey: insights from the Naples Workshop group.
items.key: This expert narrative review integrates available evidence with multidisciplinary clinical expertise to provide practical considerations for patient management while identifying areas of uncertainty and priorities for future research. Overall, management should be individualized according to disease phenotype, symptoms, reproductive potential, previous ART history, and coexisting conditions, while several commonly proposed interventions still require confirmation in well-designed prospective studies.

items.title: Genetic Diagnoses and Postnatal Outcomes in a Prenatal Cohort of Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita.
items.key:
RESULTS: Ninety-four pregnancies were included: 15 with isolated arthrogryposis, 32 with arthrogryposis and systemic anomalies excluding the central nervous system (CNS), and 47 with arthrogryposis and CNS involvement or fetal akinesia deformation sequence (FADS). Genetic findings in our cohort included 18 aneuploidies, 3 copy number variants and 25 single gene disorders. Of pregnancies with non-diagnostic cytogenetic findings that underwent next-generation sequencing (NGS), 50%…
CONCLUSIONS: AMC is genetically heterogeneous with frequent underlying single gene disorders, supporting the use of NGS in prenatal diagnosis. Neonatal morbidity and mortality remain high, particularly with FADS.

items.title: Current Status of Fetal Cardiac Care in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology Perspective: A Consensus Statement on Behalf of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology.
items.key: A risk-stratified level of care classification system is proposed. This consensus statement of the Fetal Cardiology Working Group of the German Society of Pediatric Cardiology gives an overview about the current status of fetal cardiology in Germany from a Pediatric Cardiology perspective emphasizing that detection rates in Germany stay behind in international comparison due to the minimal requirement of displaying a 4-chamber-view only in screening guidelines according to the "Mutterschaftsrichtlinie." We require mandatory views of the outflow tracts and the 3-vessel-trachea view in the 19 to 22 weeks' examination.

items.title: Head-to-Head comparison of 18F-FDG PET/MRI and 18F-FDG PET/CT for preoperative tumor staging and lymph node metastasis diagnosis in endometrial and cervical cancers: a meta-analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: This meta-analysis suggests that PET/MRI offers superior accuracy for local tumor staging compared to PET/CT in endometrial and cervical cancers, likely reflecting the inherent advantage of MRI over CT. For lymph node metastasis, the pooled point estimates for PET/MRI and PET/CT were numerically close; however, a formal paired comparison could not be performed due to the absence of discordant-pair data, and equivalence cannot be concluded. This finding nonetheless underscores the central role of the PET component for nodal detection. Given the limited number of included studies and the retrospective design of the primary studies, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and require confirmation through larger, prospective multicenter studies.

items.title: From Synapses to Circuits: A Systematic Review of How Developmental Ethanol Exposure Alters Excitation-Inhibition Balance.
items.key: In contrast, EPSC frequency varied by brain region and developmental time point, with both increases and decreases reported. No consistent directional shift emerged among studies assessing E/I balance. Developmental ethanol exposure therefore appears to alter inhibitory synaptic transmission more consistently than excitatory transmission, while its overall effects on E/I balance are heterogeneous and circuit-dependent. These findings highlight the need for systematic, region-specific, and developmentally targeted studies to clarify how altered synaptic signaling contributes to cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in FASD.

items.title: Prenatal cannabis exposure and adverse neonatal outcomes: a systematic review and meta-analysis with meta-regression on tobacco co-use.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Across more studies than any previous review, cannabis exposure was associated with small for gestational age, low birth weight, preterm birth, NICU admission and perinatal mortality. When controlling for tobacco smoking, preterm birth and NICU admission were no longer significantly increased; small for gestational age and low birth weight remained raised. Perinatal mortality showed no tobacco gradient, so is not attributable to tobacco, though balanced studies were too few. Counselling should address both substances. Evidence is observational and source-study adjustment erratic; certainty is very low and further evidence is needed.

items.title: Robotic Myomectomy for High Fibroid Burden: A Multimodal Blood-Sparing Strategy for the Removal of 40 Leiomyomas.
items.key:
