SETTING: Tertiary referral center for advanced minimally invasive gynecologic surgery.
PARTICIPANTS: A 25-year-old nulligravid woman. MRI showed a 1152-cm³ uterus with multiple leiomyomas, including an 8.6-cm dominant lesion.

items.title: Digital health interventions and maternal outcomes among pregnant women in low- and middle-income countries: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: The included papers comprised randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (n = 3), cross-sectional studies (n = 3), and mixed-methods studies (n = 2) from five LMICs. Most DHIs used smartphone technologies primarily for education, advice, and ANC reminders. DHIs improved maternal health behaviours, but evidence on clinical outcomes was inconclusive because data were…
CONCLUSION: The paper reports that DHIs improve maternal behaviours and could foster the attainment of maternal and neonatal goals in LMICs. Future research should establish the clinical outcomes associated with DHIs to inform inclusive policy responses, since equity, sustainability, and clinical outcomes remain uncertain.

items.title: What Patients are Reading About Prenatal Cell-Free DNA: An Analysis of Leading Publicly Available AI-Chatbots.
items.key:
RESULTS: Chatbot outputs varied substantially across platforms and user profiles, with misinformation, omissions, and incomplete information identified. Common themes included inconsistent explanations of the purpose and scope of cfDNA screening, frequent omission of test limitations and downstream implications, and variable readability scores (at a 9th-14th grade level)…
CONCLUSION: Publicly available chatbots may provide inaccurate or inconsistent information about cfDNA screening. As these tools are increasingly used outside clinical settings, improving accuracy, transparency, discussion of limitations, and source citation is essential to support reliable patient-facing health information.

items.title: Prenatal cell-free DNA (cfDNA) screening of chromosome abnormalities: A technical standard of the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) and the College of American Pathologists (CAP).
items.key: Multiple cfDNA analysis techniques exist, and because of the complex nature of this screening, this technical standard aims to promote uniform laboratory practices. This document deals with the technical standards applicable to prenatal cfDNA screening of chromosome abnormalities in maternal plasma. This document serves as a resource to assist clinical laboratories with the validation methods, ongoing monitoring of test quality and performance, and the interpretation and reporting of these results.

items.title: Fertility preservation and reproductive counseling in women with hereditary gynecological cancer predisposition: A scoping review of BRCA1/2 and Lynch syndrome care pathways.
items.key:
RESULTS: Of 5113 records identified, 4273 were screened after de-duplication, 280 were assessed in full, and 99 sources were included. Evidence came mainly from high-income countries and concerned BRCA1/2 carriers; 12 sources focused on Lynch syndrome. Oocyte and embryo cryopreservation were feasible, but live-birth outcomes were rarely reported. Oral contraception was associated with lower ovarian cancer risk and, in BRCA1 carriers, a…
CONCLUSION: Reproductive counseling covering fertility preservation, preimplantation genetic testing, contraception, and HRT should begin at genetic diagnosis and precede irreversible surgery. The proposed 10-step framework requires prospective evaluation.

items.title: Risk factors for metabolic syndrome: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: MetS pathophysiology is multifactorial. Comprehensive evidence shows that multiple distinct factors performed significantly associations with MetS. Unhealthy dietary patterns, sedentary behavioral patterns, and adverse occupational patterns are the primary modifiable associated factors for MetS. Despite the limited quality of current supporting evidence, targeted intervention strategies for these factors should be prioritized in public health policies to mitigate MetS at the population level. This review provides comprehensive prevention suggestions for high-risk groups.

items.title: Surgical management of cervical cancer: A Society of Gynecologic Oncology evidence-based review.
items.key: Sentinel lymph node biopsy may replace complete pelvic lymphadenectomy when an accepted algorithm is applied, with indocyanine green and near-infrared imaging the preferred mapping technique. When radical hysterectomy is indicated, the open approach is preferred outside of a clinical trial. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery is not recommended in place of chemoradiation, and hysterectomy after completion of definitive chemoradiation is not recommended in the absence of documented residual disease. Evidence quality varies considerably across questions, and several recommendations rest on observational data or expert consensus.

items.title: Risk Factors for Seven Common Aneuploidies: Successes, Limitations, Missed and New Opportunities.
items.key: Aneuploidy screening has led to early diagnosis of most affected pregnancies but has complicated the research process. The advent of cell-free DNA screening, which is simpler and maximal, could be an opportunity to refocus on understanding aetiology through epidemiology. We advocate cooperation between large population-based screening programs, revitalised birth defect registers, variant databases, and electronic medical record systems. There is a need to reap the benefits of advanced genomic technologies and combine them with traditional epidemiology to further understand aneuploidy origins.

items.title: Prevalence of human papillomavirus and HPV vaccination among cisgender bisexual women: Protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: This paper proposes a protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine whether reported HPV prevalence and vaccination rates among cisgender bisexual women differ based on whether bisexuality is defined by identity or behavior. The protocol is registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251252015) and follows PRISMA-P guidelines. Random-effects meta-analyses will estimate pooled HPV prevalence and vaccination rates by definition type. Findings will clarify how operational definitions shape observed HPV-related outcomes and inform tailored cervical cancer prevention strategies for cisgender bisexual women.

items.title: Effect of pelvic floor reconstruction on postoperative urinary continence after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a meta-analysis.
items.key: No obvious publication bias was detected. The GRADE assessment indicated that the certainty of evidence was moderate at 2 weeks and low at all other time points, primarily due to the predominance of observational studies and high heterogeneity. Pelvic floor reconstruction during RARP may improve early urinary continence recovery. However, given the low certainty of evidence, considerable heterogeneity, and the predominance of observational data, the magnitude and durability of this benefit remain uncertain. PR should be considered a reasonable option rather than a standardized intraoperative adjunct. Further high-quality, multicenter RCTs with uniform endpoints are warranted.

items.title: Non-invasive vascular assessment in gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period: a systematic review.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Non-invasive vascular assessments can help identify macrovascular, microvascular, and endothelial abnormalities in women with gestational hypertension and preeclampsia during pregnancy and the postpartum period. Although some abnormalities persist beyond delivery and may contribute to long-term cardiovascular risk, evidence remains insufficient to support their use as independent predictors of future cardiovascular events. Further standardized, prospective longitudinal studies are needed to determine their prognostic and clinical value.

items.title: Cervical Cancer Screening: Analyzing Recent Guideline Changes Against Current Trends of Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Risk Factors.

Although updated screening guidelines are supported by technological advancements and cost-effectiveness considerations, increasing trends in HPV risk factors and reduced screening adherence may limit the effectiveness of less frequent screening strategies. This narrative review analyzes cervical cancer screening guideline changes in relation to current epidemiologic trends in HPV risk factors, an important consideration when evaluating screening policy decisions.

By positioning the placenta as the primary biological interface linking maternal complications to offspring susceptibility to endocrine and complex metabolic diseases, this review provides an integrated framework for understanding developmental programming in metabolic health.

items.title: Health beliefs and parental responses to human papillomavirus vaccination in the Middle East: a theory-informed narrative synthesis guided by the health belief model.
items.key: CONCLUSION: HPV-related knowledge in ME countries remains insufficient and is frequently associated with vaccination attitudes and acceptance across the included studies. Improving uptake requires targeted educational interventions, healthcare provider engagement, public health campaigns, financial support, and policy-level initiatives. Strengthening awareness and addressing structural barriers are critical for enhancing vaccination acceptance. Self-efficacy, where directly reported, appeared to be associated with more favorable vaccine attitudes; however, direct evidence for parental self-efficacy as a distinct HBM construct was limited across the included studies and should not be overstated.

items.title: EXPRESS: Effect of inositol supplementation on plasma adipokine levels: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.key: The meta-analysis of seven randomized controlled trials revealed that inositol supplementation has no significant effect on adiponectin (WMD: 2.70 µg/mL, 95% CI: -1.02, 6.41, p = 0.12, I2 = 91%; Figure 3), leptin (WMD: 1.57 ng/mL, 95% CI: -33.28, 36.42, p = 0.66, I2 = 64%; Figure 4) or resistin (WMD: -7.43 ng/mL, 95% CI: -89.30, 74.45, p = 0.45, I2 = 94). Additionally, the sensitivity analysis was robust for adiponectin, while the effect size was sensitive to one study for each leptin and resistin. In conclusion, our results suggest that inositol supplementation has no beneficial effect on circulating adipokine levels.

items.title: Sonographically Diagnosed Adenomyosis and Hemorrhagic and Placental Complications of Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: Only two studies reported PAS, with 0/90 and 3/311 events among exposed women; these were not pooled. All studies were at serious risk of bias and certainty of evidence was very low for every outcome. When eligibility is restricted to adenomyosis diagnosed by ultrasound with explicitly reported criteria, an association with PPH is not demonstrable, and the pooled estimate depends entirely on whether the source population is symptomatic or unselected. Evidence on PAS is insufficient for synthesis. Published associations may in part reflect how cases were ascertained rather than the disease itself. Trail Registration: PROSPERO CRD420261495931.

CONCLUSIONS: Salpingotomy increased substantially following guideline revision, but one third of attempts were converted and treatment was not preferentially directed towards women with reduced tubal reserve. Preoperative ultrasound documentation frequently lacked information needed for planned tube-preserving surgery. Guideline implementation should be accompanied by targeted surgical and ultrasound training.

items.title: Efficacy of low-intensity extracorporeal shockwave therapy for erectile dysfunction: an updated systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized sham-controlled trials.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Li-ESWT may provide clinically meaningful short-term improvements in erectile function among men with probable vasculogenic erectile dysfunction. However, the magnitude of the observed effect should be interpreted with caution given the limited number of available studies and participants. Current evidence remains limited by methodological heterogeneity and relatively small sample sizes. Further high-quality multicenter trials with long-term follow-up are needed to establish the durability of treatment effects and clarify the role of Li-ESWT in clinical practice.

Findings should inform counseling that integrates frailty, comorbidity, sexual goals, functional symptoms, durability expectations, treatment burden, and patient preference.

items.title: Transvaginal flap-fistula repair with offset suturing for vesicovaginal fistula.
items.key: The urinary catheter was removed 4 weeks postoperatively, and the patient experienced no leakage. At 3-month follow-up, cystoscopy showed complete closure of the fistula. Vaginal anatomical morphology and length recovered well, with no sexual dysfunction. The Female Sexual Function Index score improved from 6 points preoperatively to 27 postprocedure. The transvaginal flap-fistula repair using an offset method can construct a robust tissue barrier and help avoid overlapping suture lines. It is a safe, effective, and minimally-invasive option that maintains vaginal length.

items.title: Predicting outcomes in locally advanced cervical cancer treated with radiotherapy: a systematic review of nomograms.

Future work should focus on robust external validation, recalibration, and evaluation in contemporary treatment cohorts before clinical implementation.

items.title: GAF Survey on the Management of Hypogonadism in Men with Concomitant Varicocele: Gaps between Real-World Practice and Current Guidelines.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Although limited by voluntary participation, an approximately 10% response rate, and recruitment predominantly from andrology-focused networks, the findings reveal substantial variation between guideline recommendations and reported real-world practice. Among responding clinicians, many consider varicocele a potentially modifiable factor in hypogonadal men and incorporate hormonal evaluation and repair into management. The findings underscore the need for adequately powered prospective studies to clarify patient selection, endocrine outcomes, and the role of varicocele in hypogonadism.

items.title: Classification of brain variants on fetal ultrasound: international Delphi consensus.

items.title: Diagnostic performance of MRI and transvaginal ultrasound for urinary tract endometriosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

For bladder endometriosis, TVUS…
CONCLUSION: TVUS and MRI show excellent specificity for diagnosing urinary tract endometriosis. MRI provides slightly higher sensitivity for ureteral disease, while both modalities demonstrate moderate sensitivity for bladder involvement. A complementary, site-specific imaging approach is, therefore, supported, with cautious interpretation of negative findings.

items.title: Global trends, regional disparities, and causes of maternal mortality - a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 513 records were identified; after removing 173 duplicates, 340 were screened. Following title and abstract review, 299 records were excluded. Forty-one full-text articles were assessed, and 30 were excluded. Eleven studies were included in the qualitative synthesis (three observational studies,…
CONCLUSION: Although maternal mortality has declined since 1990, progress has slowed and major regional inequalities persist. Indirect causes are becoming more prominent, and methodological differences complicate global estimates. Further reductions will require stronger healthcare systems, improved surveillance, and policies addressing social determinants of maternal health.

CONCLUSIONS: In this appropriately powered, randomized trial, patients experienced statistically and clinically significantly less pain with 8 weeks of nightly baclofen vaginal suppositories when compared to placebo. Baclofen suppositories were shown to be well tolerated with no adverse events.

CONCLUSIONS: Pelvic girdle pain was commonly reported during pregnancy and within the first postpartum year. However, given substantial heterogeneity and very low certainty of evidence, findings should be interpreted with caution, thereby limiting generalisability across populations.

items.title: PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors plus chemotherapy in cervical cancer: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Five phase III randomized controlled trials comprising 3,302 patients were included. The addition of PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors to chemotherapy significantly improved overall survival [HR: 0.66, 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.60-0.73] and progression-free survival (HR: 0.68, 95% CI: 0.60-0.78), with low heterogeneity I2=0%. Objective response rates was modestly increased (RR: 1.14, 95% CI: 1.02-1.26).…
CONCLUSION: PD-1-targeting immunochemotherapy prolongs survival in cervical cancer while maintaining acceptable tolerability, positioning it as a leading treatment option for eligible patients. Further biomarker-driven and head-to-head trials are needed to optimize treatment selection.

items.title: DNA methylation patterns at the IGF2-H19 locus in offspring and maternal folate intake: a systematic review.
items.key: Results for IGF2 DMR2 varied across studies, whereas associations involving blood folate biomarkers were generally weak and tissue-specific, and dietary folate intake was largely null. No observational study was judged at low overall risk of bias, and both randomized trials were assessed as having some concerns. Overall, maternal folic acid supplementation was associated with modest, region-specific differences in DNA methylation at the IGF2-H19 locus; however, methodological limitations and heterogeneity across studies preclude firm conclusions regarding the biological significance of these associations.

items.title: Acute cholecystitis during pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-based diagnosis and laparoscopic cholecystectomy appear safe across all trimesters of pregnancy, with obstetric outcomes comparable to non-operative management. Operative management was associated with a lower observed risk of venous thromboembolism, although this finding was based on limited evidence. Further prospective studies are needed to optimise patient selection and surgical timing.

items.key: CONCLUSION: Hysteroscopic morcellation is associated with high rates of complete RPOC removal and low rates of complications and intrauterine adhesions. items.title: Qualitative Interviews with PAG Fellowship Directors Support the Need to Develop a Best Practice Standard for Performing Trauma-Sensitive Pelvic Exams.

CONCLUSIONS: Findings highlight the need for consistent, evidence-informed practice standards and system-level support to integrate TSC into PAG. Developing trauma-sensitive pelvic exam guidelines could reduce re-traumatization, improve engagement, and strengthen patient-clinician trust.

items.title: Adherence to Cancer Screening Guidelines in Employer-Provided Healthcare Programs: A Survey of Companies in Lombardy (Northern Italy).

Strengthening coordination between occupational health services and public health authorities is essential to ensure appropriate, equitable, and sustainable integration of workplace-based screening initiatives into organized regional cancer prevention strategies.

items.title: Biopsychosocial correlates and predictors of sexual function in perimenopause: a systematic review.
items.key: CONCLUSION: This review demonstrates that sexual function during perimenopause is influenced by interconnected biological, psychological, and social factors. Biological changes-particularly menopause-related symptoms-play a significant role, though hormonal influences remain inconsistent. Psychological factors and relationship quality also contribute meaningfully to sexual function, underscoring the multifactorial nature of sexual health in this transitional stage. Taken together, the results of this systematic review underscore the importance of a biopsychosocial approach to understanding and addressing sexual function problems in perimenopause and highlight the need for advancing targeted research and intervention during this vulnerable period.

items.title: Nonlinear dose-response relationship between cumulative anticholinergic use and the risk of dementia in adults with overactive bladder: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis.

CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Dementia risk in OAB patients follows a non-linear trajectory, with a critical vulnerability window during the first 3 years of cumulative ACH exposure. Clinical management should prioritise non-anticholinergic alternatives (e.g. mirabegron) or implement structured cognitive surveillance during this early treatment phase.

items.title: Artificial Urinary Sphincter in Women: A Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes and Technological Evolutions.

Further prospective studies with long-term follow-up are needed to clarify the comparative effectiveness of surgical approaches, assess the impact of emerging technologies on device durability, and better characterize the effects of AUS implantation on female sexual function.

items.title: Cultural and lived experiences of menopause among women from Global Majority backgrounds in Western countries: a qualitative systematic review.
items.key: While some women described stigma, loss and disruption, others experienced greater freedom, resilience and personal transformation. These findings support the need for culturally responsive, intersectional menopause care that avoids cultural assumptions, attends to women's own understandings and treatment preferences, and strengthens clinicians' cultural awareness. Further research should include underrepresented groups and examine whether culturally adapted resources improve healthcare access, experiences and outcomes.

items.title: Perimenopause as a critical neuro-musculoskeletal window for healthy aging: integrating brain, bone and muscle health.

This narrative review critically synthesizes current evidence and proposes the bone-brain-muscle axis as an integrative conceptual framework. The model is presented as a biologically plausible clinical framework rather than a validated mechanistic pathway. Recognizing perimenopause as a potential neuro-musculoskeletal window may support earlier identification of multidimensional risk and individualized strategies to preserve physical function, cognitive health and healthy aging.

items.title: Prognostic factors of synchronous endometrial and ovarian cancers: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.

Conversely, endometrioid histology confers significantly improved survival outcomes compared to non-endometrioid types. Timely and accurate assessment of these factors at diagnosis is essential for optimizing treatment intensity and post-treatment follow-up.

items.title: Effects of e-Health interventions on psychological outcomes among high-risk pregnant women: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 42 studies, 24 (57.2%) were published after 2020, and 32 (76.2%) were randomised controlled trials. The e-Health interventions focused on psychological support (47.6%), physical health management (42.9%), and parenting role education (9.5%). The meta-analysis indicated…
CONCLUSIONS: Given their accessibility, e-Health interventions may offer potential benefits for the psychological support of high-risk pregnant women; however, these findings should be interpreted cautiously owing to the high heterogeneity in the anxiety and depression estimates. Further research is required to confirm these effects and to evaluate their optimal design, long-term effects, and cost-effectiveness.

items.title: Anorectal function after transanal natural orifice specimen extraction for colorectal cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Ten retrospective cohort studies were included, of which seven (1362 patients) contributed quantitative data for meta-analysis. Three studies contributed to the pooled Wexner incontinence score analysis and four to the pooled Pelvic Floor Distress Inventory short form (PFDI-20) analysis. At the interval…
CONCLUSION: Transanal NOSE was associated with a small, non-significant trend toward higher early Wexner scores after MIS colorectal cancer surgery, while broader pelvic floor symptom burden appeared comparable to TASE. The difference was of uncertain clinical significance, was robust to sensitivity analyses, and longer-term data suggested no persistent functional disadvantage.

items.title: Follow-up after fertility-sparing surgery for cervical cancer: should human papillomavirus testing be used routinely? A narrative review.
items.key: Currently, evidence does not support indiscriminate routine human papillomavirus testing for all patients after fertility-sparing surgery as a standalone strategy to detect invasive recurrence. However, selective use in combination with cytology and colposcopy, particularly to tailor visit frequency in patients with reassuring results after the first year, is supported by emerging evidence and is consistent with contemporary guidance. Any implementation should define management pathways for positive tests and account for the low pre-test probability of recurrence in many patients, so that harms from false positives do not outweigh benefits.

items.title: Circulating Tumor DNA and Cell-Free DNA as Candidate Biomarkers After Image-Guided Locoregional Therapy in Hepatocellular Carcinoma and Colorectal Liver Metastases: A Systematic Review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Eleven studies were included (eight HCC, three CRLM; n≈820). Pre-treatment ctDNA mutations predicted survival after TACE (CTNNB1: HR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-20.6; TP53: HR 5.3, 95% CI 1.4-10.1; KEAP1: HR 22.0, 95% CI 2.2-221.0). A cfDNA/ctDNA score stratified progression-free survival after TACE (1.3 vs 10.3 months; p=0.002). ctDNA predicted death after ablation in HCC (HR 2.6, 95% CI 1.5-4.7; p=0.001) and recurrence in CRLM (HR 2.97, 95% CI 1.47-6.03; P=0.003). Y90 evidence was limited.
CONCLUSION: CtDNA and cfDNA correlated with treatment outcomes after locoregional therapy; evidence is heterogeneous and biomarker-driven trials are required before clinical implementation.

items.title: Sedentary behaviour and female urinary incontinence. A systematic review with subtype-specific analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Eight studies (n=35 - 10,768 participants) met inclusion criteria. Greater sedentary exposure was generally associated with higher UI prevalence or severity, particularly for UUI (low-certainty evidence). Associations with UUI and UI severity appeared more consistent in accelerometry-based studies than in studies using self-reported measures, but this limited evidence…
CONCLUSION: Sedentary behaviour appears associated with UUI in women, but the direction of the association cannot be established and reverse causation is plausible. Evidence for SUI is inconclusive. Prospective studies using objective measures and subtype-specific outcomes are needed to establish temporal ordering.

items.title: Prognostic accuracy of the maternal serum IGFBP4/SHBG ratio for spontaneous preterm birth in asymptomatic pregnancies: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Seven studies from five countries (2016 to 2024) were included. Two screen-and-treat studies, one randomized, were synthesized narratively, and two studies did not report 2×2 data. For spontaneous preterm birth, the ratio alone had sensitivities of 0.75 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.43-0.95) and 0.52 (95% CI, 0.40-0.64) and…
CONCLUSIONS: The maternal serum IGFBP4/SHBG ratio shows modest prognostic accuracy for spontaneous preterm birth, based on few, partly overlapping studies funded by or involving the test developer. Accuracy data alone neither establish nor exclude clinical benefit; decisions about screening should rest on randomized evidence and independent validation.

items.title: Anti-CD38 therapy in kidney allograft antibody-mediated rejection and microvascular inflammation: a systematic review and evidence map.
items.key:
RESULTS: Thirty-seven reports were included, comprising one 22-participant randomized felzartamab trial, uncontrolled daratumumab studies and case reports, and one four-recipient isatuximab case series.…
CONCLUSIONS: One small randomized trial reported between-group differences in exploratory histologic and injury-marker outcomes at 24 weeks but did not establish benefit in kidney function or graft outcomes. Daratumumab data describe changes observed after complex rescue therapy but cannot determine an independent drug effect or prospective treatment feasibility; evidence for isatuximab is insufficient to assess efficacy. Current findings cannot be extrapolated to an anti-CD38 class effect.

items.title: Barriers limiting access to follow-up care after human papillomavirus screening for cervical cancer in global settings: a systematic review.
items.key: bout HPV results and next steps), psychological and emotional barriers (fear of treatment, stigma surrounding HPV, distrust in medical systems), social and relational barriers (partner influence, gender roles, lack of peer support), and structural and logistical barriers (transportation, costs, work conflicts). Across settings, missed follow-up after positive HPV screening appeared more strongly linked to health-system and structural barriers than lack of motivation. Strengthening referral pathways, patient tracking systems, communication of results, navigation support, and timely treatment access may improve follow-up completion and enhance the effectiveness of HPV-based screening programs.

items.title: Treatment outcome and adverse effects of new regimens (bedaquiline and linezolid) for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis during pregnancy: A systematic review.
items.key: The regimen showed favorable treatment outcomes for mothers, with treatment success rates ranging from 60.7% to 98%. However, a high incidence of adverse pregnancy outcomes was reported, including preterm birth (28%-55%), low birth weight (32%-35%), and miscarriage or stillbirth. One study reported a 35% pregnancy termination rate.ConclusionWhile the bedaquiline and linezolid regimen appears highly effective against MDR-TB in mothers, it is associated with significant adverse fetal outcomes. Close monitoring and further research are essential to determine whether the drugs or the underlying MDR-TB disease causes these outcomes.

items.title: Perimenopause and cardiometabolic risk: emerging evidence, therapeutic opportunities and unanswered questions.
items.key: Together, these findings support a model in which perimenopause represents a physiologic convergence point where symptom burden and cardiometabolic risk intersect, with implications for symptom management and primary prevention. However, major evidence gaps remain, including the absence of interventional studies during perimenopause and uncertainty regarding whether these relationships are causal or therapeutically modifiable. Future research should determine whether targeting cardiometabolic health during this window can improve both cardiovascular outcomes and the symptom experience of the menopause transition.

items.title: Twelve-Month Discontinuation of Contraceptive Methods: A Global Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: SARC users had lower odds of switching than abandoning their method (odds ratio: 0.17; 95 percent confidence interval: 0.06-0.54), whereas no significant difference was observed among LARC users. By episode use, 12-month discontinuation was 53.7 percent (n = 13,445) for SARC and 16.0 percent for LARC (n = 2,277), lower in postpartum women (8.5 percent) and higher among married women (22.5 percent). Pregnancy desire was the main reason for discontinuation among women not in need of contraception, whereas side effects predominated among those still in need. Monitoring contraceptive discontinuation is essential to guide public health policies and meet sexual and reproductive rights.

items.title: Fertility preservation for patients undergoing pelvic malignancy treatment: Current strategies, emerging approaches, and clinical considerations.
items.key: Uterine transplantation may provide a restorative option for selected patients with irreversible uterine factor infertility but remains highly specialized and resource intensive. Because each option differs in timing, evidence base, risks, costs, resource requirements, and applicability across patient groups, fertility preservation should be discussed early and incorporated into multidisciplinary cancer care. Continued research is needed to better define reproductive outcomes, pregnancy safety, complications, and comparative effectiveness of emerging approaches.

items.title: Association between breastfeeding and pelvic floor dysfunction: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Nineteen studies were retrieved for dyspareunia, eight for UI, two for POP and AI, and three for PFMF. Fourteen studies showed a significant association between breastfeeding and dyspareunia, with a greater risk of…
CONCLUSIONS: The available literature shows an association between breastfeeding and postpartum dyspareunia. However, no causal relation can be inferred. In the case of symptoms, women should be informed of the multifactorial nature of dyspareunia and of the benefits of breastfeeding. The association of breastfeeding with UI, POP and AI has not been established. Any advice to discontinue breastfeeding because of these symptoms is not supported by scientific evidence.

items.title: Gaps in Reproductive Health Counseling Among Adolescents with Chronic Medical Conditions.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 322 participants (median age 16), most reported comfort discussing birth control (76.3%) and valued subspecialty provider input (88.2%). However, only 16.1% reported discussing pregnancy-related risks with a subspecialist, and 6.8% reported being advised about pregnancy prevention in the context of their condition. While 78.9%…
CONCLUSIONS: AYAs with CMCs report low rates of reproductive health counseling despite valuing subspecialty input and reporting comfort with these discussions. Missed opportunities for counseling and confidential communication in subspecialty care may contribute to persistent reproductive health inequities for adolescents with chronic medical conditions.

items.title: Comparative Effectiveness and Safety of Treatments and Embolic Agents for Symptomatic Uterine Fibroids: A Bayesian Network Meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Twenty-three RCTs (N=2,055 women) were included. Technical success and major complication rates did not differ significantly across treatment strategies or embolic agents in the Bayesian analysis, though frequentist analysis showed slightly higher technical success with hysterectomy than UAE (RR, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.17). Myomectomy…
CONCLUSION: UAE did not differ significantly from alternative strategies in procedural success or safety, but myomectomy showed greater durability. Evidence is insufficient to establish definitive embolic-agent differences. Treatment strategy appears to influence outcomes more than embolic material, supporting individualized selection and larger trials.

items.title: Exploring associations between testosterone and cardiovascular disease in females: A systematic review.
items.key: ogical heterogeneity across the evidence base precluded meta-analyses; only 10 of the 28 studies (35.7%) quantified testosterone using gold-standard liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, only seven (25%) excluded exogenous hormone (menopause hormone therapy or oral contraceptive) users, and disease definitions, exposure metrics (total, free, bioavailable, free androgen index) and statistical models varied widely. This review highlights substantial methodological heterogeneity throughout the evidence base. We provide four addressable areas which require resolution before definitive conclusions regarding the association between testosterone and cardiovascular disease in females can be made.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Association between menstrual-related health problems and mental disorders in male partners: A nested case-control study.
items.key:
RESULTS: In total, 85,478 cases and 306,512 controls were identified. The presence of a spouse with an MRHP was associated with increased odds of a mental disorder in the male partner (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.09). These findings were consistent across sensitivity analyses. Disease-specific analyses revealed similar associations for endometriosis (OR 1.06, 95% CI 1.02-1.11) and dysmenorrhea (OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00-1.09). No significant association was observed for PMS/PMDD (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.96-1.25).
CONCLUSION: MRHPs in women, particularly endometriosis and dysmenorrhea, were modestly associated with newly diagnosed mental disorders in male partners.

CONCLUSION: Although residual confounding and concurrent changes in closure configuration, suture material/product, and treatment era preclude attribution to a specific component, the greater adjusted 3-month RMT observed in the EP group provides a hypothesis-generating anatomical signal that warrants prospective evaluation.

items.title: Evaluation of surgical outcomes and costs during the learning curve in robotic gynecologic surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: Three programs reported lower hospital costs: mean reductions of $2,222 and $4,457 and a median difference of $83 (2025 USD). Exploratory resource valuation estimated -$1,068 per case (95% CI -$3,747 to $1,610). Later phases were associated with approximately 31 minutes shorter operative time, withoperative minutes valued using an external reference input of $28.43 per minute. Available evidence didnot establish clear reductions in blood loss or hospital stay, while heterogeneous definitions precluded apooled complication estimate. The time and personal financial investment required for surgeons to reachthis stage remains an important separate cost requiring prospective evaluation.

items.title: Treatment outcomes and safety of metformin versus insulin in gestational diabetes mellitus: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: The incidence of pre-eclampsia and hypertensive disorders was similar between groups. Patient satisfaction was consistently higher in the metformin group, with most participants preferring it over insulin. Funnel plots and Egger's test indicated no significant publication bias. Metformin is a safe and effective alternative to insulin for the management of GDM in most pregnant women, offering comparable glycemic control, reduced maternal weight gain, lower risk of neonatal hypoglycemia, and higher patient acceptability. While some patients may still…

VAS pain scores were…

items.title: Venlafaxine in oncology: supportive-care evidence and emerging preclinical anticancer signals: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: 25 studies were included, comprising 23 clinical studies and 2 preclinical studies. The strongest clinical evidence supported venlafaxine for…
CONCLUSION: Venlafaxine has an established evidence-based role in supportive oncology for treatment-related hot flashes, whereas its role in CIPN and other supportive care indications remains uncertain. Emerging anticancer findings are limited to preclinical models and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Further randomized clinical trials are needed for supportive care indications, while additional mechanistic and preclinical validation is required before venlafaxine can be considered for clinical evaluation as an anticancer therapy.

items.title: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes following exposure to GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists: a time-window-stratified systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fourteen comparative data sources were included; 13 were quantitatively eligible and eight contributed to at least one pooled estimate. In the timing-specific analysis of major congenital malformations, four studies with verified periconceptional/first-trimester exposure yielded an odds ratio of 0.99…
CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear or consistent increase in major congenital malformation risk, but very low certainty, imprecision, residual confounding, heterogeneous comparators, sparse agent-specific data, and uncertain exposure timing preclude conclusions of safety. Reported preeclampsia and renal or urinary signals have not been independently replicated.

items.title: Lenvatinib starting doses below 20 mg versus 20 mg with pembrolizumab in advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of comparative observational evidence.
items.key:
RESULTS: Ten studies representing 10 independent cohorts and 1,000 patients were included. Five cohorts (703 patients in total) informed the primary starting-dose comparison, with outcome-specific analysis denominators. For starting doses below 20 mg versus 20 mg, the pooled…
CONCLUSION: Comparative observational evidence does not establish that starting lenvatinib below 20 mg preserves antitumor effectiveness or improves tolerability relative to a 20 mg starting dose. Prospective, confounder-aware comparative studies are needed before a reduced starting-dose strategy can be recommended broadly.Systematic review registration: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/, identifier CRD420261458417.

items.title: Urethroplasty for bulbomembranous strictures after benign prostatic hyperplasia surgery: systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 11 studies comprising 669 patients were identified, of which nine (417 patients) were included in the primary quantitative analysis. All studies were retrospective or prospective observational cohorts with moderate-to-serious risk of bias. Definitions of patency and continence were heterogeneous…
CONCLUSIONS: Urethroplasty for bulbomembranous strictures following BPH surgery achieves high, heterogeneously defined patency-predominantly freedom from re-intervention-with low de novo UI in experienced centres. The heterogeneous, non-comparative evidence precludes technique-specific recommendations; prospective, standardised studies are needed to refine patient selection.

items.title: Exploring the therapeutic role of Chinses herbal medicine in the recurrence rate of uterine fibroids after conservative surgery: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:

CONCLUSION: CHM is effective in avoiding recurrence of uterine fibroids after surgery, excelling in terms of overall effectiveness, restoring female hormone levels, improving hemorheological indices, and promoting uterine recovery and safety. However, these findings are preliminary and still need to be validated by higher-quality studies.

items.title: ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT PERSPECTIVES ON HOME-BASED TESTING FOR SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED INFECTIONS: A QUALITATIVE STUDY.
items.key:
RESULTS: Nine participants (42.9%) expressed comfort with home-based STI testing, citing convenience, privacy, and confidence in their ability to self-collect specimens. Many in this group viewed telehealth and in-person care as equally acceptable. Six participants (28.6%) rejected home-based…
CONCLUSIONS: Most participants demonstrated at least conditional acceptance of home-based STI testing. Successful implementation among underserved AYA may require strategies that enhance self-efficacy, address logistical barriers, and support patient choice through flexible screening pathways. These findings provide actionable guidance for expanding access to STI screening among underserved youth.

items.title: A Prospective Study of Life Impact in Five Domains During Menses in a Cohort of Early Adolescents.

RESULTS: 126 participants from 17 states with 506 documented menstrual cycles were included. Median age was 13.0 years (IQR 12,0, 14.0), and 112 (89%) had a gynecological age <3 years. Life impacts in health, extracurricular activities, and school affected approximately one in five cycles and included symptoms such as fatigue,…
CONCLUSION: Dysmenorrhea was highly prevalent in early post-menarcheal adolescents and symptoms beyond pain, such as anxiety and headaches, were frequently reported. The modified WaLIDD score was associated with life impact during menses in this population.

items.title: The psychosocial impact of living with cloacal malformations in young people: A qualitative study.
items.key:
RESULTS: Three themes were developed. Sense of the bodily self highlights the impact of treatment and symptom management on body perception and the development of sexual identity. Medical complexity reflects awareness of the complexity of the condition and treatment, interactions with medical professionals, self-management and vulnerability to medical anxiety and trauma. Growing up with…
CONCLUSION: Growing up with a cloacal malformation and the necessary treatments can significantly impact long term psychological wellbeing and identity formation. It is recommended that psychological aspects are considered as part of routine surgical and clinical care from first contact across the lifespan.

items.title: Incidence and Management of Pelvic Pain in Patients with Obstructive and Non-Obstructive Müllerian Anomalies.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 148 patients, 76 had obstructive and 72 had non-obstructive anomalies. Patients with obstructive anomalies presented younger (14.5 ± 5.0 vs. 21.1 ± 8.3 years). Pelvic pain was reported by nearly all post-pubertal patients with obstructive anomalies, and was less common among those with non-obstructive anomalies (100.0% vs. 38.9%, p<0.001). Most patients with obstructive anomalies (86.8%) were treated…
CONCLUSIONS: Obstructive Müllerian anomalies are strongly associated with earlier age of onset and presentation with pelvic pain. Persistent pain after surgery underscores the need for long-term, multidisciplinary management and further investigation into underlying mechanisms.

items.title: Assessment of treatment response response and the role of completion surgery after concurrent CRTand brachytherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer - a review from the French cervical cancer guidelines group.
items.key: Completion surgery provides no prognostic benefit and increases morbidity in patients with squamous cell carcinoma who achieve a complete response after CRT and brachytherapy. Evidence remains insufficient to establish its role in adenocarcinoma. When completion surgery is indicated, delaying the procedure until at least 6-8 weeks after CRT may reduce postoperative morbidity. Simple hysterectomy should be favored over radical hysterectomy, which increases morbidity without improving survival. Current evidence demonstrates no superiority of minimally invasive surgery or laparotomy in terms of oncologic outcomes or overall morbidity.

items.title: Comparative effectiveness of luteal phase support strategies in natural cycle frozen-thawed embryo transfer: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

The RCT-only NMA could not be performed because the network was disconnected, with no closed loops among the 8 RCTs, reflecting the…
CONCLUSION: LPS was associated with improved pregnancy outcomes in NC-FET. The RCT-only network was too sparse to support valid rankings. While VP + triptorelin ( ± hCG) showed relatively high SUCRA values for CPR and LBR, the very low certainty of evidence precludes definitive conclusions.

CONCLUSIONS: FIGO 2023 m demonstrated superior prognostic discrimination compared with FIGO 2009, supporting incorporation of molecular subtypes into routine endometrial cancer staging and risk assessment. Clinically, this integrated framework may help identify patients at risk of under- or over-treatment, particularly in those with disease previously considered as early stage, although prospective studies are needed before treatment algorithms can be changed definitively.

items.title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
items.key:
There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients.

items.title: Short and long-term outcomes after gestational diabetes diagnosis using different glycemic criteria: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:

Lower diagnostic criteria or thresholds, compared with higher diagnostic criteria or thresholds, doubled GDM diagnosis and pharmacotherapy use, increased neonatal hypoglycemia (RCTs: 18 more per 1,000; 95% CI 11 to 25 more) and maternal-neonatal separation (RCTs: 6 more per 1,000; 95% CI 1 to 12…
CONCLUSIONS: Lower diagnostic criteria increased the diagnosis of GDM and some aspects of healthcare utilization, without improving short-term outcomes. Limited evidence suggested possible longer-term benefits, warranting further long-term follow-up from high-quality RCTs.

items.title: Survival After Risk-Reducing Mastectomy in Patients With Pathogenic Variants in BRCA1 and BRCA2: A Network Meta-Analysis.
items.key:

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this systematic review and network meta-analysis of RRSO-adjusted analyses, RRM was associated with lower all-cause mortality compared with breast cancer screening among females with PVs in BRCA1 and BRCA2, with the greatest magnitude of association for breast cancer-specific mortality observed in BRCA1 PV carriers. These findings provide less confounded survival estimates to support individualized shared decision-making for RRM.

items.title: Electroacupuncture for Mild-to-Moderate Stress Urinary Incontinence in Women: A Systematic Review.
items.key:

CONCLUSIONS: Based on small-scale Chinese trials, EA appears more effective than sham EA, medication, or pelvic floor muscle training (PFMT) in reducing urine leakage and improving ICIQ-SF scores, with superior long-term effects. However, due to limited, low-quality evidence restricted to Chinese populations, we cannot conclusively demonstrate EA's superiority over PFMT or pharmacotherapy for mild-to-moderate SUI in women.

items.title: Metabolic, hormonal, and reproductive effects of GLP-1 receptor agonizts in hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant women: a systematic review.
items.key:

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 receptor agonizts are a promising adjunctive therapy in hyperandrogenic insulin-resistant states, with the strongest evidence for metabolic improvement. Further high-quality, phenotype-specific trials are required.

items.title: Learning Curve, Training, and Operator Experience in Vaginoscopic Hysteroscopy: A Systematic Review.
items.key: However, procedural speed, overall outpatient hysteroscopy proficiency, and vaginoscopy-specific competence were not assessed consistently, and the available evidence did not establish a validated, universal case-number threshold for independent vaginoscopic cervical access. No included clinical study established an individualized competency threshold for vaginoscopic access using sequential learning-curve methodology. These findings favor multidimensional, performance-based assessment rather than reliance on procedure counts alone and support prospective studies with standardized success criteria and individualized monitoring.

items.title: Artificial intelligence in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy: a systematic review.

CONCLUSIONS: The available studies suggest that AI may support the automation of selected workflow steps and assist treatment-related decision-making in image-guided cervical interventional radiotherapy. While several applications have achieved high technical performance, most remain at the proof-of-concept stage, and robust external validation and prospective clinical evaluation are needed before routine clinical adoption.

items.title: The role of artificial intelligence in predicting late-onset intrauterine growth restriction in singleton pregnancies: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

CONCLUSION: AI/ML models showed high pooled discriminative accuracy for late-onset IUGR. However, the evidence derives mainly from retrospective, single-center case-control studies without external validation; calibration was reported in six of 19 studies and decision-curve analysis in none. items.title: Effects of selenium supplementation on glycemic indices and oxidative-stress biomarkers in adults: a systematic review, meta-analysis, and dose-response analysis of randomized controlled trials.

CONCLUSIONS: Selenium supplementation was associated with modest improvements in insulin-sensitivity markers, selected antioxidantand…

items.title: The impact of menstruation-related symptoms on women's quality of life, work productivity, and economic burden: a structured narrative review.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 86 studies were used to inform the thematic synthesis. Across conditions, menstruation-related disorders were consistently associated with reduced health-related QOL, psychological distress, and…
CONCLUSIONS: This review highlights the multidimensional burden of menstruation-related disorders extending from physical symptoms to mental health and functional outcomes. The predominance of presenteeism suggested that conventional metrics based on absenteeism underestimate the true societal impact. The observed gap between symptom improvement and functional recovery underscored the need for integrated approaches that could address both clinical and psychosocial pathways.

items.title: Hysteroscopic vs. laparoscopic management of cesarian scar defect: a meta-analysis.

items.title: Pregnancy considerations in women with uncorrected tetralogy of Fallot.
items.key: Contemporary data from the ESC EORP Registry of Pregnancy and Cardiac Disease (ROPAC) report maternal mortality of 0.7% and heart failure in 8.7% of pregnancies with uncorrected congenital heart disease, with markedly worse outcomes in cyanotic subsets. This narrative review synthesizes the pathophysiology, risk stratification, obstetric management, intrapartum anesthetic considerations, comparative outcomes of uncorrected versus corrected disease, and key evidence gaps that continue to constrain care for this population, providing a physiology-driven framework for the pregnancy heart team.

items.title: The gut-ovary axis in polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome: Mechanisms, microbiome dysbiosis, and emerging therapeutic strategies.
items.key: Microbiome-targeted interventions, including probiotics, prebiotics, synbiotics, and dietary approaches, show potential, whereas fecal microbiota transplantation remains largely experimental. Conventional metabolic therapies, including glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, should be considered separately from microbiome-targeted approaches. Overall, the gut-ovary axis represents a promising framework for understanding the systemic features of PMOS, but substantial heterogeneity, limited longitudinal human evidence, and underrepresentation of diverse populations currently limit translation into clinical practice.

items.title: Polycystic ovary syndrome research in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review on current status and future directions.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: PCOS remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa, with substantial gaps in population-based epidemiology, diagnostic practices, phenotype distribution, management, and metabolic outcomes. Addressing these gaps through larger, well-designed studies is critical to accurately assess the disease burden, inform clinical guidelines, and optimize management strategies. Additionally, overcoming barriers such as cultural attitudes, cost, and limited accessibility to diagnostic tools and treatment options remains essential to improving PCOS care and research across the region.PROSPERO registration ID CRD420250649730 - 13 March 2025.

items.title: Carbohydrate Quality Versus Quantity in Gestational Diabetes Mellitus While Considering Randomized Dietary Interventions: A Systematic Review.
items.key: With only two or three small trials per pool, I² = 0% does not indicate homogeneity. Fiber, staple-quality, and provided-diet interventions improved selected postprandial measures, but obstetric, birth-size, and neonatal-adiposity benefits were not established, and certainty was low or very low. Carbohydrate quality is a plausible route to postprandial improvement without aggressive restriction, but current randomized evidence does not establish a universal quality-over-quantity rule or support lower carbohydrate intake as superior. Carbohydrate amount should be individualized while prioritizing nutrient-dense, lower-glycemic-index, fiber-rich sources.

items.title: Access to Early Pregnancy Assessment Clinics and Guideline-Recommended Investigations for Recurrent Pregnancy Loss in Ontario.
items.key: Little is also known regarding EPACs' integration of recurrent pregnancy loss (RPL) care, impacting up to 5% of patients. We surveyed Ontario obstetrics and gynaecology chiefs (May-October 2025, 33 responses, 61% response rate), and found 50% had EPACs and 15% had RPL protocols. Access to RPL investigations varied: gynaecologic ultrasound (89%), antiphospholipid antibody testing (85%), products of conception testing (54%), parental karyotyping (39%), and 3D ultrasound/sonohysterography (31%). We advocate for greater EPACs access, and integrated RPL protocols to improve patient care.

items.title: International expert consensus on the contemporary role of pelvic exenteration in recurrent or persistent cervical cancer.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: The role of pelvic exenteration in recurrent or persistent cervical cancer has evolved within an increasingly multidisciplinary and personalized treatment landscape. Contemporary expert opinion supports prioritizing modern systemic therapies and re-irradiation strategies over pelvic exenteration initially. Nevertheless, pelvic exenteration continues to represent a potentially curative option in carefully selected patients when complete resection is achievable and non-surgical alternatives have failed, are not feasible, or are unlikely to provide durable local control.

items.title: Brucella abortus RB51 vaccination: a comprehensive systematic review of safety, efficacy, and global field outcomes (1990-2025).
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: RB51 preserves DIVA capability and induces cell-mediated immunity under ideal conditions but carries significant risks, including vaccine-induced abortion, milk shedding, and incomplete cross-protection. Its safety and effectiveness are highly context-dependent, performing well in low-prevalence countries with robust test-and-slaughter programs but failing in high-endemicity settings where pregnant adults are routinely vaccinated. Strict contraindication of RB51 in pregnant animals, pasteurization of dairy products from vaccinated herds, and complementary use of species-specific diagnostic tests are urgently needed. RB51 should not be used as a stand-alone intervention, and its continued use in endemic regions with mixed Brucella species requires re-evaluation.

items.title: The Impact of High Intensity Focused Ultrasound on Ovarian Reserve in Women with Uterine Fibroids and Adenomyosis: A Systematic Review and Single Arm Meta-Analysis.
items.key: Pooled single-arm analysis showed a small but statistically significant reduction in serum AMH levels following HIFU treatment, with no significant change in AFC. This decline was associated with, rather than proven to be caused by, HIFU treatment, as the available evidence derives predominantly from uncontrolled pre-post studies that cannot establish causality. Therefore, evaluation of ovarian reserve after HIFU should not rely on AMH alone but incorporate AFC and clinical context. Pre-treatment counseling is particularly important in women with diminished ovarian reserve or of late reproductive age, in whom even minor reductions may be clinically relevant.

items.title: Wearable Electrohysterography Systems: A Systematic Review of Electrode Topology, Design Considerations, and Clinical Feasibility.
items.key: The reviewed literature indicates that configurations employing approximately 8-16 electrodes represent a practical range for balancing spatial characterization and clinical usability. However, the findings reveal persistent challenges related to the limited integration of electrode design, signal acquisition, and analytical methods. This evidence underscores the need for an integrated approach that considers flexible electrode interfaces, standardized electrode configurations, and adaptive signal processing techniques. By aligning technological improvements with clinical requirements, this study identifies practical considerations for developing wearable maternal-fetal monitoring systems.

items.title: Integrated Molecular Classification of Endometrial Cancer: Impact on Diagnosis, Prognosis, and Clinical Management-A Systematic Review.

RESULTS: Fifty studies were included. Of these, 13 provided data on molecular subtype distribution (comprising 3527 patients), 8 reported survival outcomes, and 7 reported hazard ratios. CONCLUSIONS: Integrated molecular classification is an essential tool for prognostic stratification and treatment personalization in endometrial cancer. items.title: Plasma and Serum Metagenomic Sequencing of Microbial Cell-Free Nucleic Acids for Suspected Central Nervous System Infection: A Systematic Review.
items.key: All five plasma-only detections came from single case reports, which contributed to no yield or agreement denominator; excluding the four abstract-level case reports moved no proportion by more than 1.3 percentage points. RNA viruses, low-burden focal mould disease, and chromosomally integrated HHV-6 were recurrent sources of false-negative or misleading results. Conclusions: Plasma or serum metagenomic sequencing is a useful adjunct in selected difficult CNS infections, particularly disseminated, fungal, amoebic, or fastidious bacterial disease, but it does not replace CNS-site diagnostics.

items.title: Genomic Profile of Asian Women with Recurrent Implantation Failure: A Systematic Review.

VEGF emerged as the most consistently associated gene, highlighting the importance of endometrial vascular remodeling in implantation success. Larger, multi-ethnic genomic studies with functional validation, together with a standardized definition of RIF, are warranted to clarify these associations and advance personalized reproductive medicine in ART.

items.title: Transfusion Management in Pregnancies Complicated by Hemoglobinopathies: Evidence, Guidelines, and Clinical Challenges.

items.title: Surgery-related factors predisposing to uterine niche after cesarean section: a systematic review.
items.key: The aspect of single- and double-layer uterine closure remains under debate, as most studies do not show the superiority of either technique with regard to uterine niche incidence. All patients undergoing cesarean delivery should be screened for cesarean scar defects and informed about the potential complications of cesarean section.

items.title: Metformin Use During Pregnancy and Early-Life Nutritional Status: A Systematic Review of Randomized Clinical Trials.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence does not consistently support an effect of prenatal metformin exposure on early infant anthropometry. Limited postnatal data and absent adiposity measures limit conclusions regarding postnatal growth and early metabolic programming and support standardized longitudinal body composition assessment.

items.key: Overall, 0.32% (n = 6179) of pregnancies were exposed to AOMs. Prevalence was highest among women aged > 40 years (1.1%) and those with pre-pregnancy obesity or type 2 diabetes (1.4% and 1.2%, respectively). Overall exposure increased modestly from 2018 to 2022, followed by a marked rise between 2022 (0.31%) and 2023 (0.58%). Prior to 2023, most exposures involved phentermine; in 2023, semaglutide accounted for the highest prevalence. The results highlight the need for further research to evaluate maternal and fetal outcomes associated with AOM exposure.

items.title: Maternal RSV Vaccination and Complementary Infant-Protection Strategies in Singapore: A Modified Nominal Group Technique Consensus Study.

items.title: From Germ Cell Histogenesis to Precision Risk Stratification: Prognostic and Predictive Molecular Markers in Testicular Germ Cell Tumors-A Systematic Review.

items.title: Joint Hypermobility and Female Lower Urinary Tract Symptoms: A Systematic Review.

items.title: Recombinant activated factor VIIa for severe postpartum hemorrhage in Africa: Evidence, appropriate use, and research priorities-A narrative review.
items.key: The indication remains unapproved by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and is off-label in most other African countries. Efficacy depends on timely administration after definitive obstetric source control and correction of coagulopathy and physiological derangements. Current evidence supports rFVIIa as a protocolized rescue adjunct rather than routine therapy. In Africa, its use should be restricted to carefully selected women with refractory PPH managed in tertiary centers with multidisciplinary expertise. African registries, pragmatic implementation studies, and health-economic evaluations are needed to define its optimal role within resource-constrained healthcare systems.

items.title: Antenatal diagnosis and classification for placenta accreta (adherence) spectrum: Clinical practice guideline and recommendations by the World Association of Perinatal Medicine and the Perinatal Medicine Foundation.
items.key: Two-dimensional grayscale ultrasound is the mainstay of antenatal assessment, supported by color Doppler; three-dimensional imaging may provide additional information in selected specialist settings. Magnetic resonance imaging has a complementary role when ultrasound is inconclusive, placental location is non-anterior or non-previa, or technical factors limit visualization. Suspected CSP or PAS should prompt referral to a perinatal center with multidisciplinary expertise, blood product support, adult and neonatal intensive care, and access to complex pelvic surgery. Delivery timing and surgical preparation should be individualized.

items.title: School, community, family, clinic, and technology-based approaches to adolescent pregnancy prevention: a comprehensive systematic review.
items.key: Community programs demonstrated moderate improvements in contraceptive use and delayed sexual initiation at 6-12 months. Only intensive family-based interventions with structured reinforcement reduced pregnancy rates at ≥12 months. Knowledge improvement does not guarantee a reduction in pregnancy. Sustained impact depends on intervention intensity, reinforcement, and long-term follow-up, supporting integrated multicomponent strategies with standardised pregnancy indicators.

items.title: Screening for maternal infection in pregnancy to prevent preterm birth: a systematic review.

items.title: From Dysbiosis to Malignancy: The Female Genital Tract Microbiome in Endometrial Cancer; Insights from a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Female genital tract microbial dysbiosis is associated with EC, characterized particularly by depletion of potentially protective microorganisms and enrichment of potentially pathogenic or infection-associated taxa. These microbial alterations may have potential as adjunctive biomarkers for EC risk stratification and early detection. However, the available observational evidence does not establish a causal role of microbial dysbiosis or infection in endometrial carcinogenesis. Large prospective studies using standardized sampling, sequencing, and analytical methods are required to clarify causality and determine the clinical utility of microbiome-based diagnostic and therapeutic approaches.

It will help classify CRS according to its complexity clarifying formulation of recommendations for perioperative care.

CONCLUSIONS: Maternal circulating sST2 is elevated in established PE, but evidence of elevation before clinical onset is limited and diagnostic accuracy is uncertain. sST2 cannot currently be recommended for the prediction or diagnosis of PE, and prospective studies with standardized assays, gestational-age-specific thresholds and evaluation of incremental value over the sFlt-1/PlGF ratio are required.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Impact of artificial intelligence in embryo selection to improve pregnancy rates per transfer in IVF cycles: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Ten studies were included. Only two reported arm-level outcomes suitable for meta-analysis. The pooled estimate showed no significant difference in clinical pregnancy rate between…
CONCLUSION: AI-based embryo scoring showed no statistically significant difference compared with conventional morphology for per-transfer clinical pregnancy rate, with potential advantages in standardization and inter-observer consistency. However, superiority remains unconfirmed and key patient-centered outcomes including cumulative live birth rate, miscarriage rate, and time-to-pregnancy were not reported in available studies. Larger multicenter RCTs with standardized outcome reporting are required.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: IVF outcomes after transvaginal sclerotherapy for ovarian endometrioma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Low-certainty evidence suggests that pre-IVF ethanol sclerotherapy for ovarian endometrioma may be associated with improved clinical pregnancy compared with expectant management, with benefits evident regardless of prior cystectomy history. While a positive trend in live births was observed, this finding was not statistically significant at the patient level, highlighting the fragility of the current evidence. These clinical enhancements are supported by overall improvements in oocyte and embryo yields. Sclerotherapy serves as a valuable, fertility-preserving alternative to repeat surgery for selected patients.

items.title: Effectiveness of prophylactic subcutaneous negative-pressure drainage for the prevention of surgical site infection in gynaecological cancer patients with BMI ≥ 35 kg/m2: a multicentre open-label randomized trial.
items.key:
RESULTS: Data from 191 patients were analysed. Median BMI was 39 kg/m2. The incidence of SSI was comparable between the drainage and control groups (15.5% vs 14.9%; p = 0.913). Drain…
CONCLUSION: Subcutaneous negative-pressure drainage did not significantly reduce the incidence of SSI following abdominal hysterectomy in morbidly obese patients with gynaecological cancer. Of all predefined secondary outcomes, only postoperative wound haematoma was reduced significantly. Conversely, both the unadjusted and adjusted analyses suggested a potential increase in postoperative fever, although significance was not reached. As these were secondary outcomes, they should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: Association of mode of delivery with postpartum disease flares in women with inflammatory rheumatic diseases.

RESULTS: Postpartum flares occurred in 247 patients (57.0%), more frequently after CS than VD (67.7% vs 44.8%, p < 0.001). In primary multivariable logistic regression analysis, CS remained significantly associated with higher odds of postpartum flare (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]…
CONCLUSION: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk and earlier occurrence of postpartum flares in women with IRDs after adjusting for demographic, disease, and therapeutic covariates. While these observational findings highlight mode of delivery as a potential factor associated with postpartum disease course, confirmation in prospective studies is required before influencing routine clinical practice.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Maternal and neonatal outcomes in pregnancies with cystic fibrosis after lung transplantation or during elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) therapy: a single-center descriptive cohort.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 95 pregnancies in 46 women, 56 resulted in live births, including 7 after LT and 10 during ETI therapy. In the LT cohort, pre-existing comorbidities were frequent: cystic fibrosis-related diabetes (CFRD) (100%), chronic…
CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world cohort, ETI-exposed pregnancies were associated with reassuring maternal and neonatal outcomes, while pregnancies after LT were characterized by frequent transplant-related and vascular morbidity; the two groups were described separately and were not formally compared. These findings support the need for multidisciplinary follow-up and prospective registries to evaluate maternal and pediatric outcomes in the CFTR modulator era.

The MHC…
CONCLUSIONS: Emergency caesarean, multiparity, current professional activity, gestational age at delivery, and perceived quality of prenatal care were associated with changes in HRQoL postpartum. These associations should be interpreted with caution because some observed differences did not reach the minimal clinically important difference.

items.title: Cervical cancer: ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for diagnosis, treatment and follow-up.
items.key: • This ESMO CPG provides key recommendations and algorithms for managing cervical cancer. • Treatment and management algorithms for locoregional and recurrent/metastatic disease are provided based on the latest data. • Includes new surgical treatment recommendations for early-stage, locally advanced, and recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer. • Recommendations are based on available scientific data and the authors’ collective expert opinion. • The ESMO-MCBS scores and LoE/GoRs describe the evidence for treatment and can aid with setting choice priorities.

items.title: Bladder neck vs midurethral placement of autologous retropubic fascial slings: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: We screened 5578 abstracts, assessed 233 full texts for eligibility, and retained 61 studies. Of the 61 studies, 13 were randomized controlled trials and 48 were observational studies. Objective (74.0% vs 81.1%; odds ratio, 1.10 [95% confidence interval, 0.37-3.28]) and subjective cure (70.8% vs 58.6 %; odds ratio 0.46 [95% confidence interval, 0.19-1.10]) were not statistically significantly different…
CONCLUSION: Bladder neck and midurethral placements of autologous fascial slings have similar rates of surgical success and adverse effects, except for de novo urgency, which favors midurethral sling placement. A randomized controlled trial is required to confirm these findings.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Ovarian reserve and miscarriage risk outside assisted reproduction: a large cohort study.

RESULTS: Among 6,827 women reporting previous pregnancy, 4,141 (60.7 %) reported at least one miscarriage. AMH distribution differed across pregnancy history groups; however, associations observed in unadjusted analyses between moderately low or high AMH and miscarriage were attenuated after multivariable adjustment. Age-adjusted AMH z-scores demonstrated no clear…
CONCLUSION: In this large cohort, outside assisted reproduction settings, age-adjusted AMH was not independently associated with miscarriage history or miscarriage rate. These findings suggest ovarian reserve should not be used to retrospectively explain pregnancy loss or infer miscarriage risk in women outside ART settings.

items.title: Low-grade serous ovarian cancer: 2026 expert consensus report.
items.key: mutated LGSOC, emerging evidence supporting endocrine therapy combined with CDK4/6 inhibition, and refined guidance for biomarker-directed treatment selection, imaging assessment, toxicity management, and patient-centered survivorship. The panel emphasizes treatment-specific biomarker interpretation, multidisciplinary care, central pathology review for clinical trials, and the continued need for prospective studies addressing treatment sequencing, predictive biomarkers, and quality-of-life outcomes. This updated international consensus provides an evidence-based framework for the diagnosis and management of LGSOC while identifying priorities for future clinical research and drug development.
