CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS: The pooled prevalence of PCCL was high. Additionally, early first sexual intercourse, parity, STIs, multiple sexual partners, smoking, oral contraceptive use, CD4 count, and ART were positively associated with the occurrence of PCCL. Therefore, stakeholders shall implement interventions to avert future incidents of PCCL and address the identified factors.

items.title: Anatomical Variations and Morphometry of the Pudendal Nerve: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: This meta-analysis highlights the substantial anatomical variability of the pudendal nerve, which limits the feasibility of a single, universally applicable classification system. A comprehensive understanding of its morphology and branching patterns is essential for improving the safety and effectiveness of surgical and anesthetic procedures in the pelvic region. The findings emphasize the need for standardized methodologies and nomenclature in future anatomical studies to enhance comparability and clinical applicability. Ultimately, improved anatomical knowledge of the pudendal nerve may contribute to better diagnostic accuracy and reduced risk of iatrogenic injury.

items.title: Performance of AI-based models in prenatal detection of trisomy 21 via ultrasonography: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Nineteen studies published between 2015 and 2026 were included: eight image-based classifiers, seven marker-based risk models, and four enabling-task studies.…
CONCLUSION: Reported performance of AI models for trisomy 21 is high but comes mostly from retrospective, internally validated studies, and benefits for screening performance, invasive testing, or operator dependence have not been demonstrated. No study compared AI with cell-free DNA screening, so the role of these tools within current screening pathways remains undefined. Prospective, multicenter validation with karyotype-confirmed outcomes and standardized reporting is needed before clinical integration can be supported.

items.title: Comorbidities and outcomes associated with young adult hip fracture: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Forty-four studies were included from 1875 eligible abstracts. Twenty-three studies reported data on question 1. Psychiatric disease (15% [10-23%]), glucocorticoid exposure (5% [2-14%]), psychotropic exposure (12% [3-42%]), alcohol excess (15% [6-38%]) and cigarette smoking (36% [25-49%]) were highly prevalent in YAs with hip fracture. Twenty-six studies…
CONCLUSION: Psychiatric morbidity, alcohol excess and smoking were the major risk factors associated with hip fracture in YAs. Further research is required to establish the risk factors for minimal trauma hip fracture in YAs. Limited data on mortality in YAs following hip fracture are concerning and deserve further investigation.

items.title: Beyond antifracture efficacy: Osteoanabolic versus antiresorptive therapy for chronic pain after osteoporotic vertebral fractures. A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: Combined exploratory meta-analysis of RCTs and NRSIs favored osteoanabolic therapy, but in association with very high heterogeneity and no robustness in sensitivity analyses, thus just regarded as hypothesis-generating. Future studies should clarify the pathophysiological mechanisms of persistent pain following OVFs and their correlation with different clinical phenotypes predictive of differential responses to antifracture therapies. The applied protocol for this systematic review/meta-analysis was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number: CRD420261281929).

Total…
CONCLUSIONS: Severe complications following repair of primary UPOP are infrequent. Abdominal MIS carry higher risk of bowel injury, with lower risk of transfusion compared to vaginal approaches. These data should inform shared decision-making for surgeons and patients considering surgical repair for primary UPOP.

items.title: Diagnostic Performance of cfDNA-Based Liquid Biopsy for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

As exploratory observations, methylation-based assays with relatively higher sensitivity may have potential value for screening high-risk populations, while fragmentomics-based assays with relatively favorable specificity may aid differential diagnosis. items.title: Changes in the diagnosis and management of polycystic ovary syndrome in adolescents based on recommendations of scientific societies over the last decade.
items.key:
RESULTS: In adolescents with PCOS, clinical symptoms of hyperandrogenism and menstrual irregularities are the main diagnostic criteria, whereas polycystic ovarian morphology and anti-Müllerian hormone concentration are not considered reliable indicators in adolescents. The current approach to PCOS also emphasizes the assessment and management of…
CONCLUSIONS: The diagnosis and treatment of PCOS in girls require a separate approach related to age and ongoing puberty. According to the latest recommendations, lifestyle changes should be a mandatory part of therapy regardless of the background of the presented disorder. The pharmacological treatment should be tailored to the dominant symptoms.

items.title: Fertility evaluation of infertile women: a committee opinion.
items.key: Diagnostic evaluation for infertility in women should be conducted in a systematic, expeditious, and cost-effective manner to identify all the relevant factors with an initial emphasis on the least invasive methods for detecting the most common causes of infertility. The purpose of this committee opinion is to provide a critical review of the current methods and procedures for the evaluation of infertile women, and it replaces the document of the same name, last published in 2021 (Fertil Steril 2021;116:1255-65).

items.title: Progesterone Receptor Antagonists for Labor Induction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Use of mifepristone for labor induction was associated with reduced odds of cesarean delivery, as well as improved cervical ripening and labor induction efficiency. No evidence of short-term maternal or neonatal risk was found, although…

items.title: Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation: a systematic review of surgical techniques, donor safety, and recipient outcomes.
items.key: Robotic-assisted living-donor hysterectomy for uterus transplantation appears technically feasible and has been associated with viable grafts and successful pregnancies in highly selected cases. However, major donor complications, including ureteric injury requiring reimplantation and bilateral oophorectomy, were observed, and the true incidence of donor morbidity remains uncertain. Current evidence remains limited to small observational studies, and these findings support careful evaluation within structured, multidisciplinary programmes and international registries rather than widespread expansion.

items.title: Lifestyle factors associated with hot flash frequency and daily interference: highlighting the role of sleep quality, diet quality and physical activity.

For HFF, each one-category worsening in sleep quality was associated with higher odds of being in a higher frequency category (adjusted odds ratio [aOR]=2.44; P =0.001); older age was inversely associated (aOR=0.42; P =0.002). CONCLUSION: Findings suggest the importance of routine sleep quality for symptom burden and may inform lifestyle-focused approaches to symptom management.

items.title: A Review of Guidelines for the Use of Tranexamic Acid in the Management of Postpartum Hemorrhage and Assessment of Associated Maternal Outcomes.
items.key: It pays particular attention to differences in how these guidelines position TXA within PPH treatment pathways and integrate it with other first-response interventions. This review also considers uncertainties around prophylactic use, alternative hemostatic therapies, and variation in guideline implementation. Greater consistency in evidence-based recommendations may clarify TXA's role in contemporary PPH management while allowing flexibility for differences in healthcare settings and resources.

items.title: Early apical release versus conventional (non-early apical release) holmium laser enucleation of the prostate: a systematic review and meta-analysis of postoperative urinary incontinence and functional outcomes.

At mid-term follow-up, 3-4 months, EAR was associated with lower risk of SUI (RR 0.44, 95%CI 0.28-0.69; I² = 0%). At 6-12 months, there were no significant differences in urinary incontinence. EAR had fewer intraoperative and late postoperative complications. However, EAR showed more early postoperative complications, mainly Clavien-Dindo grade…
CONCLUSION: EAR reduces early SUI while maintaining comparable functional outcomes compared to conventional HoLEP. These findings indicate EAR is an effective continence-optimizing modification during HoLEP.

items.title: Functional and Surgical Outcomes of Nerve-Sparing Approaches in Deep Infiltrating Endometriosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Nerve-sparing surgery for DIE appears feasible and is associated with acceptable surgical and functional outcomes. However, the current evidence is limited, and substantial heterogeneity precludes conclusions regarding equivalence or superiority compared with conventional surgery. Further well-designed prospective and comparative studies are needed.

RESULTS: 12 population-based cohort studies including over 11 million women were analyzed. Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy were associated with higher long-term risk of AF (HR 1.50; 95 % CI 1.38-1.62), as was preeclampsia (HR 1.45; 95 % CI 1.23-1.71). Preterm birth was also associated with increased AF risk (HR 1.29; 95 % CI 1.13-1.48). Delivery of a large for gestational age…
CONCLUSION: Hypertensive and vascular pregnancy complications are associated with elevated long-term maternal AF risk. Associations for gestational diabetes and fetal growth phenotypes were heterogeneous and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support APOs as markers of later arrhythmic vulnerability.

CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative PFMT may improve short- and long-term continence recovery after RP. Certainty was very low for the heterogeneous short-term evidence and low for the long-term evidence; differences by surgical approach remain inconclusive.

items.title: Biological Grafts for the Surgical Management of Uterovaginal Prolapse: A Narrative Overview of the Evolution of Biomaterials.
items.key: Each option available today requires a trade-off. Native-tissue repair avoids graft-related complications, but recurrence remains an important problem for some patients. Permanent synthetic implants provide durable structural support, but can cause material-specific complications. Biological grafts have not consistently improved long-term outcomes. New materials are therefore needed that balance mechanical support, tissue integration, and biologic compatibility. We conclude by focusing the attention of the clinical and scientific communities on the scarcity of rigorous comparative trials and on this unmet need in the field of female pelvic medicine.

items.title: Eligibility and prescribing of low-dose aspirin for preeclampsia prevention under two international guidelines: a retrospective cohort study.

The overall agreement between the two guidelines was 82.9 %, with moderate concordance (Cohen's kappa=0.50). McNemar's test demonstrated a significant difference in patient classification (p<0.001). Aspirin…
CONCLUSIONS: Although the ACOG guideline identified substantially more women as eligible for aspirin prophylaxis than the NICE guideline, documented aspirin prescribing remained considerably lower than guideline-defined eligibility, highlighting an implementation gap in routine clinical practice.

CONCLUSIONS: GLP-1 receptor agonists show promising preliminary signals for improving spontaneous conception in women with PCOS, but the available evidence remains limited. CONCLUSIONS: RPL guidelines exhibit important methodological and clinical heterogeneity that extends beyond differences in the available evidence. items.title: Systematic Review of Pregnancy After Myomectomy: The Risk of Uterine Rupture.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 13,381 pregnant women with a history of myomectomy were included. The estimated overall risk of uterine rupture during pregnancy and labour was 0.30% (40/13.381; 95% CI: 0.21-0.41). CONCLUSION: This systematic review found an incidence of uterine rupture during pregnancy and labour of 0.30% after a previous myomectomy. Entry into the uterine cavity during myomectomy appears to significantly increase the risk. Large, high-quality prospective studies are needed to confirm this finding and to identify additional risk factors.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Human mollicutes- a silent cause of pelvic infections and associated infertility - a review.
items.key: Traditionally, these organisms are not screened for in the workup of subfertile couples; hence, the burden of their association with infertility remains largely unknown, and they may be one of the many pieces in the puzzle of unexplained infertility. This review looks at the current evidence linking Mycoplasma spp. and Ureaplasma spp. to infertility in both women and men, outlines possible pathogenic mechanisms, and evaluates whether screening for these organisms should be incorporated into the work-up of subfertility.

items.title: The relationship between endometrial cancer and urinary incontinence: systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Six studies comprising 955 patients and 85 healthcare professionals met inclusion criteria. The collective evidence reveals that UI is a highly prevalent yet often undermanaged consequence of EC and its…
CONCLUSION: Due to common risk factors, direct effects of the disease, and damage from therapy, urinary incontinence is a common and clinically important side effect of endometrial cancer and its therapies. As the number of EC survivors keeps rising, addressing UI must become a priority in comprehensive survivorship care. Future efforts should focus on developing validated screening tools, establishing evidence-based management guidelines, and implementing integrated care models.

Prospective validation is required to evaluate their clinical impact and refine areas of ongoing uncertainty.

items.title: Plastics in human reproductive tissues: A systematic review of detection, characterization, and effects on fertility.

CONCLUSION: The findings of this review show that MPs and NPs accumulate in human reproductive tissues and may induce cellular dysfunction. CONCLUSION: Lower serum sulfated GAGs, particularly the heparan sulfate fraction, were associated with impaired placental hemodynamics in PE but tracked overall disease severity. These observational findings are limited by the method and are hypothesis-generating; they require replication with disaccharide-level profiling.

items.title: Optimal exercise modalities and doses for blood pressure management in adults with prehypertension and hypertension: A systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 284 randomized controlled trials, including 18,750 participants with a mean age of 56.8 years, covering ten exercise modalities were included. Aquatic exercise achieved the greatest reduction in systolic blood pressure, with a mean difference of -10.28 mmHg and a 95% credible interval from -13.05 to -7.49; the surface under the cumulative ranking curve was 93.26%. Whole-body…
CONCLUSION: Ten exercise modalities were associated with reductions in blood pressure, with particularly strong effects for aquatic, mind-body, and isometric exercise at specific doses. These findings may inform more tailored exercise prescription strategies for adults across hypertension phenotypes.

items.title: Methodological heterogeneity as a confounding variable in reported trends in human sperm parameters: a critical reappraisal.
items.key: y, I contend that the apparent decline in sperm parameters is, in large part, an artefact of comparing heterogeneous data generated by methodologically non-equivalent assessment techniques across time or geography. Differences in manual versus computer-assisted sperm analysis, evolving World Health Organization reference criteria, laboratory standardization, population sampling strategies and controls over abstinence intervals collectively introduce systematic variance that can mimic or amplify the appearance of biological deterioration. Until these methodological confounders are rigorously partitioned from biological signals, conclusions about genuine spermatogenic decline remain premature.

items.title: Atovaquone-proguanil chemoprophylaxis during pregnancy: a case series and a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Our case series included 191 AP-exposed pregnancies (133 during first-trimester (T1) and 75 during second/third trimester) resulting in 85.9% livebirths (n=164), 10.0% miscarriages (n=19), 1.0% medical abortions (n=2), 1.0% stillbirth (n=2) and 2.1% elective termination (n=4). The prevalence of MCA…
CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that pregnancy outcomes and MCA following AP chemoprophylaxis exposure are similar to the general population prevalences, with a low level of evidence. These data strengthen the evidence supporting a reassuring safety profile, and AP may represent a reasonable option for pregnant women requiring malaria chemoprophylaxis after risk-benefit assessment.

items.title: Non-invasive diagnosis of endometriosis: From expert imaging to molecular and artificial intelligence-enabled pathways.
items.key: No blood, urinary, or endometrial biomarker meets criteria for clinical use; circulating miRNA panels have failed independent validation, and a salivary miRNA signature still needs independent, lower-prevalence validation. Radiomics and AI remain investigational pending external validation, calibration, and demonstrated clinical utility. Non-invasive diagnosis is best framed not as one replacement test but as a multimodal, staged pathway in which each tool is used according to how far its evidence has progressed, which shortens diagnostic delay, targets specialist care, and interprets a negative scan safely.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Discriminative performance of plasma urea, creatinine, and uric acid for severe preeclampsia: a cross-sectional study.
items.key:
RESULTS: Eighty-four women (44.2%) had severe preeclampsia. All three biomarkers were higher in the severe group (p < 0.001 each). AUCs were 0.71 (95% CI 0.63-0.78) for urea, 0.69 (0.62-0.77) for creatinine, and 0.73 (0.65-0.80) for uric acid; pairwise AUC differences were not significant (all p ≥ 0.46). Urea ≥4.34 mmol/L had 63.1%…
CONCLUSIONS: These routinely available biomarkers showed modest discrimination of severe preeclampsia. Uric acid was highly specific at the selected cut-off but had low sensitivity, and no biomarker had a superior AUC. The data-driven cut-offs are exploratory and require external validation. They should supplement, not replace, clinical severity assessment.

items.title: Synergies between time-lapse imaging and PGT to optimize laboratory workflow and clinical outcomes.
items.key: While both technologies can be effective individually, their combined application may offer a synergistic approach that addresses the limitations of each method when used in isolation. The integration of TLI and PGT may allow for a more informed and accurate embryo ranking. This synergy has the potential to improve implantation rates, clinical pregnancy outcomes and live birth rates, while also supporting single-embryo transfer strategies and reducing associated risks. This article reviews the current understanding of the combined use of TLI and PGT. It highlights their clinical advantages, limitations and future potential in optimizing outcomes and workflow in ART.

items.title: Effectiveness of non-pharmacological interventions on stress and anxiety management in pregnancy: a systematic review.
items.key: This review provides a comprehensive overview of interventions which prevent or manage prenatal stress, anxiety and fear of childbirth. However, heterogeneity across studies made comparisons of effectiveness impossible. Greater standardization is needed in future studies. Specific populations such as coparents and specific medical conditions such as participants with psychiatric comorbidities must be included in future studies. Finally, a reduction in the risk of bias is required to allow findings to inform clinical practice.

items.title: 2025 European Society of Cardiology guidelines for the management of cardiovascular disease and pregnancy : Statement of endorsement by the NVVC.
items.key: This article contextualises the 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) guidelines for managing cardiovascular disease (CVD) and pregnancy in the Netherlands. The guideline addendum provides additional recommendations for situations where the ESC guidelines may not fully align with Dutch clinical practice. By endorsing the ESC guidelines through this addendum, the Netherlands Society of Cardiology (Nederlandse Vereniging Voor Cardiologie) supports its members in adhering to evidence-based management strategies for CVD and pregnancy.

items.title: Comparison of fecal continence and bowel function scoring systems following anorectal malformation repair: a systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Fifteen studies published from 2012 to 2025, with individual sample sizes of 20-267 participants, were included. Krickenbeck was used in 14 studies (93%) and Kelly in nine (60%). Only one study, based on 39…
CONCLUSION: The limited available evidence suggests that commonly used ARM bowel function instruments may yield non-equivalent information, but it is insufficient to establish their interchangeability or the superiority of any single system. Krickenbeck is currently the most frequently used instrument. Prospective comparative studies using standardized administration and appropriate agreement analyses are needed before a universal core instrument can be recommended.

items.title: Polymers for Pelvic Floor Repair: Current State and Future Prospects.
items.key:
RESULTS: Permanent materials covered include polypropylene, polyvinylidene fluoride, polytetrafluoroethylene, polyethylene terephthalate, polyamide, and polyurethane. Resorbable materials include lactide- and caprolactone-based polyesters, polydioxanone, polyhydroxyalkanoates (notably poly-4-hydroxybutyrate), and natural polymers such as silk fibroin, bacterial cellulose, and collagen. The use of advanced manufacturing techniques and…
CONCLUSIONS: The review provides a reference point for the design of next-generation urogynecologic implants, which requires integrated consideration of polymer properties, scaffold architecture, and host biology across the course of tissue remodeling.

items.title: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline: Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms.
items.key:
Included studies underwent quality assessment, and a modified GRADE (Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation) evidence-to-decision framework was applied to interpret and translate the evidence into recommendation statements.
RECOMMENDATIONS: This Clinical Practice Guideline includes recommendations on pharmacologic and nonpharmacologic interventions for the management of menopause-related vasomotor, sleep, and mood symptoms. Recommendations are classified by strength and evidence quality. Ungraded Good Practice Points are included to provide clinical guidance when a formal recommendation could not be made because of inadequate or nonexistent evidence.

items.title: 'Efficacy and safety outcomes after slings or artificial urinary sphincter implantation for non-neurogenic male stress urinary incontinence: a systematic review' for more clarity.
items.key:
RESULTS: Of 133 references screened, after exclusion of duplicates, 18 papers were eligible for a full-text analysis and 9 studies (5921 patients) were included in the qualitative synthesis. Among these, one was a randomized controlled…
CONCLUSION: In comparative studies, continence proportions were generally higher after artificial urinary sphincter implantation, while the complication profiles of the two devices differ, with more erosion after the sphincter and more urinary retention after the sling. Confidence in these findings is limited by clinical heterogeneity, confounding by indication and inconsistent outcome definitions. Standardised outcome reporting and randomised data are needed.

items.title: Efficacy and Safety of Lidocaine Compared to Other Agents for Intrauterine Device Insertion Pain: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key:
MAIN RESULTS: Six studies (N = 658) compared lidocaine to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) or misoprostol. Of these, two studies showed statistically significant pain reduction with lidocaine versus NSAIDs (study 1: 5.4 ± 2.8 vs. 7.3 ± 2.1, p < 0.001; study 2: 2.6 ± 0.9 vs. 4.1 ± 1.1, p < 0.001). The…
CONCLUSIONS: Lidocaine did not demonstrate a statistically significant reduction in pain. It remains unclear whether lidocaine, NSAIDs, and misoprostol are clinically comparable options. Secondary outcomes varied, and safety data were limited, highlighting the need for standardized endpoints. Further head-to-head trials are needed to guide optimal pain management for IUD insertion.

items.title: 2022 WHO estimates for overall and human papillomavirus test-based cervical cancer screening coverage worldwide: a review and synthetic analysis.
items.key:
FINDINGS: Cervical cancer screening recommendations were identified in 161 (80%) of 202 countries, with 92 (57%) of 161 countries recommending HPV test-based screening. By 2022, global coverage for women aged 30-49 years using any screening method (ie, cytology, HPV test, visual inspection with acetic acid, or combinations of these methods) was estimated at 19% (95% CI 15-22) for the previous year, 31% (26-35) in the previous 3 years, and 35% (30-39) in the previous 5 years; and 38% (33-43) of…
INTERPRETATION: Despite policy updates, overall and HPV-specific screening coverage remains far below WHO's 70% target. Three in five women aged 30-49 years worldwide have never been screened, and…

items.title: Successful introduction of a one-step blastocyst warming protocol: a UK multicentre large cohort comparison.
items.key:
RESULTS: A total of 3887 blastocysts were warmed, with a significantly higher survival rate after OSW (97.7%) than after standard warming (95.9%; chi-squared[1] = 10.84, P = 0.013). No significant differences were observed in clinical pregnancy rates (OSW: 44.7%; standard warming: 41.2%; P = 0.088) or live birth rates among cycles with a recorded final outcome (OSW: 35.8%;…
CONCLUSION: One-step warming protocols improve blastocyst survival rates with no effect on clinical outcomes. Standard warming takes about 10 times longer per embryo than the OSW protocol, which enables clinics to significantly improve laboratory efficiency and resource management without compromising patient care.

items.title: Relationship between trophectoderm re-biopsy and serum beta-HCG levels in early pregnancies.
items.key:
RESULTS: On day 9 after FET, the re-biopsy group had significantly lower mean β-HCG (111.4 ± 69.0 mIU/ml) compared with the single biopsy (149.6 ± 70.2 mIU/m; P =0.011) and no biopsy (152.5 ± 80.3 mIU/ml, P = 0.008. On day 11 after FET, re-biopsy had significantly lower mean β-HCG (221.2 ± 208.7 mIU/m) compared with single biopsy (433.6 ±…
CONCLUSIONS: Trophectoderm re-biopsy was associated with significantly lower β-HCG in early pregnancies resulting in live births without corresponding differences in perinatal outcomes. These findings suggest that β-HCG levels after re-biopsied FET may require contextual interpretation, as lower levels do not necessarily reflect a compromised prognosis.

CONCLUSIONS: YouTube videos on LBC showed limited educational quality and reliability. Important procedural details were frequently missing. Higher-quality, standardized videos may improve the educational value of online content for clinicians and patients.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Hydrocephalus-related amenorrhoea: A scoping review.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Hydrocephalus-associated amenorrhoea, most often due to aqueductal stenosis, likely reflects hypothalamic GnRH disruption from ventricular dilation. Surgical decompression usually restores menstrual cycles, though timing varies with baseline pubertal status. Early recognition is critical in adolescents with unexplained hypogonadotropic hypogonadism; because menstruation may resume quickly postoperatively, preoperative contraceptive counselling is advised in postpubertal patients. These findings underscore the need for multidisciplinary management and further research into long-term endocrine and reproductive outcomes.

items.title: Prevalence of urinary incontinence among women in Turkey: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key: Forty-five studies published between 2005 and 2025, including 41,038 participants, were analyzed. The pooled prevalence of UI among women aged 15 years and older was 36.7%. Prevalence estimates for stress, urgency, and mixed UI were 31.1%, 18.4%, and 27.5%. Definitions used influenced prevalence rates. Planning and delivering appropriate health services based on these findings can contribute to protecting and improving women's health. In Türkiye, it would be beneficial to develop a policy to raise awareness about urinary incontinence in women and to evaluate the condition. Interventions can be implemented nationwide in this way.

items.title: Clinical, economic, and health-related quality of life impact of intrapartum group B Streptococcus (GBS) tests for prevention of neonatal GBS infection: a systematic literature review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Clinical evidence demonstrated that intrapartum PCR tests provide high diagnostic accuracy and operational reliability by delivering results in <60 min (significantly faster than antenatal cultures). Four assays (Xpert® GBS, Revogene® DBS GS, GenomEra®, and IDI-Strep B™) met the European clinical expert consensus criteria for reliable and effective intrapartum GBS screening (≥90% sensitivity and ≥95%…
CONCLUSION: Point-of-care intrapartum PCR-based screening methods offer potential to improve prevention strategies for neonatal infection and reduce the clinical, economic, and HRQoL burden of GBS disease. Limited primary HRQoL evidence highlights the need for further research.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Emotional recognition deficits in pregnancy-onset Bell's Palsy.
items.key:
RESULTS: 79.5% of patients developed palsy in the third trimester of pregnancy. Sequelae was common, with 59% of patients requiring botulinum toxin injections. Emotion recognition accuracy was significantly reduced compared to normative data (Z=-2.35; p= 0.019), 6 patients had pathological scores. Greater smile asymmetry was associated with poorer emotion recognition (n = 39, r = -0.367, p = 0.021). No significant links were found between emotion recognition and anxiety or affectivity questionnaire scores.
CONCLUSION: Facial palsy occurring during pregnancy or puerperium is associated with long-term facial dysfunction and reduced ability to recognize emotions on others' faces.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Cervical lacerations are more frequently observed in nulliparas with obstetric anal sphincter injuries: evidence from a large cohort.
items.key:
RESULTS: Among 22,220 term singleton cephalic deliveries reaching full cervical dilatation, 102 cases (0.46%) were complicated by OASIS. Cervical lacerations were significantly more frequent in women with OASIS compared to those without (4.0% vs. 0.4%, p < 0.001). When stratified by parity, this association was only evident among nulliparous women: 6.1%…
CONCLUSION: Cervical lacerations were more frequently observed among nulliparous women with OASIS, suggesting a pattern of concurrent birth canal trauma. Incorporating routine cervical inspection during OASIS repair, particularly when performed in the operating theatre, may help reduce underdiagnosis of concurrent injury in this population.

In the RFA group, 15.2% experienced surgical failure compared with 3.8% in the myomectomy group (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 4.17; 95% CI, 1.39-12.50), and 46.4% experienced composite failure in the RFA group compared with 25.5% in the myomectomy group (aOR 3.18; 95% CI,…
CONCLUSION: Laparoscopic RFA of leiomyomata is associated with higher odds of surgical and composite failure compared with laparoscopic myomectomy at 2 years, even after adjusting for baseline differences between groups.

items.title: Menopausal hormone therapy combined with antiresorptive therapy for skeletal outcomes in postmenopausal women: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In postmenopausal women, systemic MHT, bisphosphonate therapy, and their combination improved BMD compared with control. Combination MHT plus bisphosphonate therapy showed the most favorable hip-region BMD profile; however, current evidence is insufficient to establish superior fracture prevention or long-term safety.

items.title: Premature menopause and risk of type 2 diabetes among postmenopausal women: findings from the Women's Health Initiative.

RESULTS: Premature menopause (n=13,230; 9.7%) was associated with a higher risk of T2D compared with menopause at ages 50-54 (hazard ratio [HR]: 1.10; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.05-1.16). Elevated risks were observed among women who never used HT (HR: 1.24; 95% CI: 1.08-1.42) or used estrogen plus progestogen (HR: 1.35; 95% CI: 1.09-1.68), but not among estrogen-only users. BMI mediated (indirect effect:…
CONCLUSIONS: Premature menopause was modestly associated with an increased T2D risk; this association varied by HT use and was partially mediated by BMI.

items.title: Quantitative assessment of neurokinin receptor antagonists in menopausal hot flashes: a model-based meta-analysis.
items.key:
FINDINGS: These studies evaluated two NK3-RAs: fezolinetant and elinzanetant. Both agents demonstrated a rapid onset of action, with efficacy reaching a plateau shortly after initiation, and exhibited clear dose-response relationships. When the dose of fezolinetant was…
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Fezolinetant (45 mg) and elinzanetant (120 mg) demonstrated comparable efficacy for menopausal hot flashes. Model-based indirect comparisons provided clinical context for interpreting their efficacy relative to other hormone and nonhormone therapies. This study provides quantitative evidence to inform medication selection and pharmacoeconomic evaluations in women with menopausal hot flashes.

items.title: Effects of adherence to a Mediterranean diet on body weight in postmenopausal women: a systematic review.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: The different design, limited number of studies and their small sample sizes may have limited the strength of evidence, making the detection of long-term benefits difficult. In qualitative synthesis, the included studies showed mixed findings, with no consistent superiority of MedDiet across weight, fat mass, or lean mass outcomes. MedDiet counseling alone, without explicit energy restriction or other structured weight-management strategies, should not be assumed to produce clinically meaningful reductions in body weight or fat mass.

items.title: The effectiveness of physical activity interventions on non-physiological symptoms of menopause: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
items.key:
FINDINGS: Twelve RCTs involving 1,003 women were included. PA significantly improved depression (g=-1.37, 95% CI [-1.96 to -0.79], mood (g= 0.84, 95% CI [0.40-1.29]), psychological QoL (g=0.66, 95% CI [0.19-1.13]), and overall QoL (g=1.10, 95% CI [0.32-1.88]). Significant reductions in depression were found in both perimenopause (g=-1.57, 95% CI [-2.58 to -0.56]) and early postmenopause…
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: PA may seem to improve depression, mood, and QoL in women in the MT. Both ABIs and MBIs may be beneficial, supporting the integration of PA into clinical care for menopausal women. Further high-quality trials with clearer menopause staging are needed to strengthen the evidence base.

items.title: Risk Factors for Recurrence Following Surgery for Apical Prolapse: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
items.key:
RESULTS: Of the 4,149 abstracts screened, 25 studies (14,860 women; median follow-up 24 months) met the eligibility criteria. Meta-analyses were performed for 9 of the 16 risk factors identified. Advanced preoperative prolapse stage (OR 2.75; 95% CI 1.39-5.46), prior prolapse surgery (OR 2.09; 95% CI 1.16-3.75), and higher body mass index (BMI; OR 1.10 per unit increase; 95% CI 1.06-1.15) were…
CONCLUSIONS: Advanced preoperative prolapse stage, prior prolapse surgery, and higher BMI were each significantly associated with U-POP recurrence. Together with expert consensus, these findings should inform preoperative counseling and individualized surgical planning to improve long-term outcomes.

items.title: The impact and value of [18F]-FDG PET-CT on management of patients with cervical cancer with service evaluation audited against national evidence-based PET-CT guidelines.
items.key:
RESULTS: [18F]-FDG PET-CT identified new metastatic sites in 16/59 (27.1%) scans. The remaining scans were concordant with the CT and MRI. The majority, 57/59 (96.6%), of the scans were performed in accordance with the guidelines. The management plan was changed by 5/59 scans (8.4%), confirmed by 48/59 (81.4%) and was not impacted with 6/59 (10.2%) scans.
CONCLUSION: [18F]-FDG PET-CT is superior to conventional imaging and enhances the management plan. Future cohort studies with larger patient numbers involving multicentric studies are needed to fully assess its impact on cervical cancer management and prognosis.

items.title: THE Environmental Impact of Contraceptive Methods - A Systematic Review.
items.key: Overall, the included studies reported on only a limited range of environmental impacts, such as waste production, carbon footprint and ecotoxicity, while overlooking other aspects of environmental sustainability. Because of this no definitive conclusions or comparisons could be made based on the full environmental sustainability. However, by extending the focus beyond direct environmental impacts towards overall sustainability, different contraceptive groups were ranked according to their overall sustainability. This led to the conclusion that long-acting reversible contraceptives are relatively more sustainable then short-acting reversible methods.

items.title: The ameliorative effect of active ingredients of traditional Chinese medicine on male reproductive injury: A review.
items.key: CONCLUSION: Extensive experiments have been performed to investigate the effects of active ingredients and herbal formulas on improving male reproductive dysfunction, revealing that TCM has the potential to combat male reproductive dysfunction through multi-level, multi-target mechanisms. However, there is a lack of reviews addressing the causes of male reproductive dysfunction and related treatment approaches. Therefore, this review aims to summarize current research progress in the use of TCM to combat male reproductive dysfunction, thereby providing a theoretical foundation for future preclinical validation and clinical application in the treatment of male reproductive dysfunction.

items.ta: Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol
items.title: Psychological distress in pregnant women undergoing prolonged hospitalization: A prospective observational study.
items.key:
RESULTS: Depressive and anxiety symptoms were frequent in the study population. An EPDS score ≥ 10 was observed in 69.5% of participants, while 60.2% scored ≥ 12. Overall,…
CONCLUSIONS: Pregnant women undergoing prolonged antepartum hospitalization showed a high burden of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Psychosocial factors, particularly recent stressful life events, were associated with greater symptom severity. These findings support the potential value of systematic mental health screening and timely psychological assessment in hospitalized obstetric populations. Further controlled studies are needed to clarify the independent contribution of hospitalization to psychological distress.

items.title: Digital health technologies for the prevention and management of urinary tract infections in menopausal women: A systematic review.
items.key:
RESULTS: Of 9935 records identified, 14 studies met the inclusion criteria. Certainty of evidence ranged from very low to moderate. Four technology clusters emerged: patient-facing digital…
CONCLUSIONS: Digital health technologies show potential for antimicrobial stewardship in menopausal women with urinary tract infections but remain largely insensitive to menopause-specific biological factors. One randomised controlled trial demonstrated increased uptake of vaginal oestrogen therapy with the use of these technologies, providing evidence of digitally supported non-antibiotic prevention. Future research should integrate menopausal staging, hormonal variables, and user-centred design.

items.title: Structured reporting of diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders: an ESGE-ESHRE-IFFS international consensus†ǂ.
items.key:
MAIN RESULTS AND THE ROLE OF CHANCE: The document provides a structured reporting of hysteroscopic findings into five sections, each systematically capturing patient characteristics, procedural findings, and pathological observations as follows: patient's characteristics, and findings from the vagina, cervix, uterine cavity, endometrium, and tubal ostia.
SUMMARY ANSWER: This collaborative document by the European Society for Gynaecological Endoscopy (ESGE), the ESHRE, and the International Federation of Fertility Societies (IFFS) provides the first detailed structured reporting template for diagnostic hysteroscopy findings in women with reproductive disorders.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence in Prediction and Diagnosis of Fetal Growth Restriction: A Systematic Review.
items.key: AST assessment showed that the risk of bias was low for the participant, predictor and outcome domains, but the analytical domain raised methodological concerns; nine studies were low risk, 14 moderate and 4 high. The AI and ML models for FGR detection performed promisingly. Multimodal approaches that combine clinical, imaging and molecular data consistently outperform single modality models and constitute a major advance in precision obstetrics. However, there remains substantial heterogeneity, limited external validation and methodological issues. Future prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, and real-world implementation research are needed for routine clinical adoption.

items.title: Vaccination for girls and women across the life course: Evidence-based recommendations for clinical practice and policy.
items.key: Vaccines reviewed include HPV, tetanus-diphtheria-pertussis (Tdap), influenza, hepatitis B, measles-mumps-rubella (MMR), varicella, herpes zoster, pneumococcal, Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV), and COVID-19. A life-course framework is proposed, emphasizing maternal immunization, cervical cancer prevention, and integration of regular and opportune vaccination into routine obstetric and gynecologic services. Practical implementation strategies and policy recommendations are outlined to support FIGO member societies.

items.title: Behavioral treatment of urinary incontinence: a guideline-driven narrative review.
items.key: CONCLUSIONS: Behavioral therapy provides a safe, effective, and highly adaptable foundation for UI management across diverse populations and care settings. Despite heterogeneity in study design, intervention protocols, and outcome reporting, international guidelines consistently endorse conservative strategies as first-line treatment. Future research should prioritize intervention standardization, harmonized outcome frameworks, inclusion of underrepresented groups, and integration of implementation science and digital health innovations to maximize long-term effectiveness and global uptake.

items.title: Cell-Free Fetal DNA Testing for Single Gene Conditions (Scientific Impact Paper No. 80).
items.key: This is known as cell-free fetal DNA (cffDNA) and so is a potential source of genetic material that can be used to test the baby for selected genetic conditions. Discovery of cffDNA in the mother's blood now allows for testing for genetic conditions as early as the 8th week of pregnancy, commonly referred to as non-invasive prenatal diagnosis (NIPD). Its use has evolved in clinical practice from 2011 when it was originally developed to screen for common chromosome differences such as Down, Edwards and Patau syndromes and for this purpose is referred to as non-invasive prenatal screening or testing…

items.title: Plasma metabolomic profiles associated with breastfeeding history and subsequent ovarian cancer risk.
items.key:
RESULTS: The highest quartile of metabolite-based breastfeeding score was inversely associated with ovarian cancer risk (meta-analyzed odds ratio [OR] = 0.62, 95% CI = 0.39 to 0.99). Of the 14 individual metabolites associated with breastfeeding in NHS/NHSII and also measured in VDAART, similar direction of associations was observed for 11 metabolites. Phosphatidylcholines (PCs; NES = 1.94; FDR = 0.004) and phosphatidylethanolamines (PEs; NES = 1.82; FDR = 0.01) were positively…
CONCLUSION: Our results suggest alterations of systemic metabolism, particularly among PC and PE pathways, provide insight into biological pathways underlying the inverse breastfeeding-ovarian cancer association.

items.title: Necroptosis as a key player in cervical cancer progression and management: a systematic review and transcriptomic cross-study consensus analysis.
items.key: These findings position necroptosis as a promising target for combination therapy strategies aimed at converting immunologically "cold" tumors into more responsive phenotypes. By integrating published signatures with exploratory analyses, we identify potential avenues to modulate necroptotic signaling in ways that may enhance synergy with immunotherapies, and have synthesized a hypothetical cell signaling and interaction diagram. Collectively, this work provides a foundation for future experimental validation and therapeutic development.

items.title: RETRACTION: Effect of Follicular Diameter at the Time of Ovulation Triggering on Pregnancy Outcomes During Intrauterine Insemination.
items.key: The p-value for ongoing pregnancy or for livebirth is reported as 0.013 in Table 3. However, re-calculation of the p-value results in a non-significant result (p = 0.1228), when comparing the 19-20 mm group to the other groups. As a result, the reported conclusions are considered unreliable, since this re-calculation of the p-value differs from those used by the authors to support their conclusions. As a result, the Editor-in-Chief has lost confidence in the data and conclusions of the article. Therefore, a retraction is warranted. When informed of the decision to retract, M.A. Maher on behalf of the authors, disagreed with this outcome.

items.title: Digital Interventions for Frailty and Pelvic Floor Dysfunction in Older Adults: A Systematic Review Protocol.
items.key: Published condition-specific reviews suggest that digital interventions may improve selected outcomes in PFD or frailty populations, but certainty varies, and those findings cannot be extrapolated to a dual-condition population. Accordingly, representative results are presented as a condition-specific evidence map and synthesis-decision framework; no pooled dual-condition effect, network estimate, or treatment ranking is reported. The protocol emphasizes traceable study identification, population alignment, outcome compatibility, and a prespecified gate for pairwise or network meta-analysis.

items.title: Faith-based organisations in providing HIV services within low- and middle-income countries (LMICs): a systematic review.
items.key:

CONCLUSIONS: Despite cultural and resource-based challenges, FBO interventions showed significant potential for expanding community-based HIV care within LMICs in sub-Saharan Africa. This review discusses several recommendations to strengthen FBO activities, encourage effective partnerships with FBOs, and ultimately lead to better HIV outcomes within LMICs. However, given the heterogeneity and quality of studies included, recommendations should be interpreted with caution.

items.title: An Update on microRNAs as Noninvasive Diagnostic Markers for Endometriosis: Why Have We Not Reached Consensus?
items.key: From the studies presented in this review, although several miRNAs have emerged as candidate biomarkers, there is still considerable variability with respect to differentially expressed miRNAs between women with and without endometriosis. Focused assessment of the methodologies used to isolate serum/plasma, extract RNA/miRNAs, amplify and normalize data from these samples, as well as whether and how sample hemolysis was assessed, revealed differences among the studies, all of which impact miRNA profiles. As such, it is imperative to develop a standardized protocol when assessing miRNAs from blood if we hope to identify miRNAs that may prove useful in noninvasive diagnosis of endometriosis.

items.title: Historical Evolution of Pelvic Exenteration Surgery in Gynecologic Cancers: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Brunschwig's Era versus Contemporary Practice.
items.key:

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with the original Brunschwig era, contemporary pelvic exenteration is associated with substantially lower major morbidity and perioperative mortality, together with improved oncologic outcomes. These findings illustrate the remarkable technical and conceptual evolution of pelvic exenteration over the past seven decades, although direct comparisons between historical and contemporary series should be interpreted cautiously because of differences in patient selection and clinical practice over time.

items.title: Fertility counseling and preservation considerations in patients with gynecologic and non-gynecologic BRCA and Lynch-associated malignancies.
items.key: In helping these patients, oncologists must navigate the following areas of care: cancer prevention, impact of cancer prevention strategies on fertility, impact of cancer treatment on fertility, effective cancer therapies, and preservation of fertility without compromising oncologic outcomes. This intersectionality between fertility preservation and effective cancer prevention/therapy makes the care of these patients extremely complex. With the utility of multidisciplinary care models, careful employment of evolving new treatment strategies, it is possible for patients to achieve their fertility desires while at the same time being protected from the risks imposed by their genetic mutations.

items.title: Diagnostic accuracy of circulating blood biomarker families in acute ischemic stroke: a secondary grouped meta-analysis with primary-study verification.
items.key:
RESULTS: Seventeen verified primary reports published from 2003 to 2025 contributed 24 original diagnostic test estimates. The cohort-level primary dataset contained 17 independent cohorts. Extracellular chromatin/cell-free DNA tests (four cohorts) yielded…
CONCLUSION: Non-coding RNA and extracellular chromatin/cell-free DNA tests show promising but methodologically fragile diagnostic signals. The evidence is not sufficient for routine clinical implementation because realistic stroke-mimic cohorts are sparse, thresholds are usually data-driven, and reconstructed cells and within-cohort multiple testing remain important limitations. Prospective one-gate, mimic-enriched validation is required.

items.title: Outcomes of robotic-assisted excision of paratubal cysts in a pediatric cohort: A multicentric retrospective study and systematic review.

RESULTS: Twenty-seven girls underwent robotic cystectomy for cysts measuring 11-176 mm (median 50 mm). Median age was 14 years, with median weight of 56 kg. Median operative time was 88 min. No conversions occurred. Median hospital stay was 2 days (range 1-4), with no complications at median…
CONCLUSIONS: Robotic-assisted surgery appears safe and feasible for paratubal cyst excision in selected pediatric patients, offering precision and minimally invasive access, with favorable perioperative outcomes and preservation of adnexal anatomy. It may support fertility preservation, however evidence regarding long-term reproductive outcomes are lacking and further prospective studies are required.

items.title: The hormonal management of adults with gender incongruence: what the non-specialist Endocrinologist needs to know. A position statement from the Society for Endocrinology.

This position statement supports minimal effective hormone dosing when appropriate, and the adoption of pragmatic strategies in later life or palliative contexts. A coordinated, patient-centred approach is key to optimizing long-term outcomes and ensuring safe, effective continuation of gender-affirming care.

items.title: Vaginal natural orifice transluminal endoscopic myomectomy.

Generalizability and long-term reproductive outcomes remain uncertain, as there is need for more robust evidence from comparative studies.

CONCLUSIONS: Psychosocial distress in pregnancy with fetal anomaly is multidimensional, arising from the interaction of emotional responses, social pressures, and healthcare experiences, and extends beyond symptoms of mental health diagnoses. This framework provides a foundation for tailored screening approaches and intervention development to support patient-centered maternal-fetal care.

CONCLUSION: Women with earlier or later menarche tended to have a higher risk of infertility than those with average menarche. However, confidence intervals were also compatible with no association. No associations were observed for age at voice break and infertility among men.

The development and implementation of consistent international evidence-based practice guidelines for the prompt diagnosis and management of MC twin pregnancies and their associated complications may contribute to more favorable outcomes.

items.title: Vaccinations in pregnancy: An update for a changing time.
items.key: While national immunization schedules vary, there is broad international consensus recommending influenza and tetanus-diphtheria-acellular pertussis (Tdap) vaccination during pregnancy, with increasing adoption of maternal respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) immunization. This review provides an updated, globally relevant summary of recommended vaccines before, during, and after pregnancy, highlights vaccines under development, and discusses implementation challenges. Strengthening maternal immunization requires coordinated action across governments, healthcare systems, industry, and media to improve access, trust, and equity in vaccine delivery.

items.title: Oral contraceptive use and anterior cruciate ligament injury or reconstruction in women: A systematic review and meta-analysis of very low-certainty evidence.
items.key:
RESULTS: Ten studies were included; seven were meta-analysed. The primary analysis (four studies) showed no clear association (OR, 0.89; 95% CI, 0.77-1.02; I…
CONCLUSIONS: The primary adjusted or matched analysis did not establish a clear association between oral contraceptive use and anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction or operatively treated injury; substantial heterogeneity, residual confounding and very low certainty of evidence preclude causal interpretation. Current evidence does not support initiating or selecting oral contraceptives for anterior cruciate ligament injury prevention. Well-designed prospective studies with standardised exposure and outcome definitions are needed.

items.key: CONCLUSION: AM and EPs are repeatedly identified together across diverse gynecological pathways, but the observed likelihood of identifying the alternative lesion is strongly pathway-dependent. Identification of one lesion should not end diagnostic consideration when symptoms, imaging findings, infertility, or treatment response remain incompletely explained. Current evidence supports targeted consideration of the alternative lesion, with further evaluation guided by symptoms and clinical pathway, rather than universal dual-pathology screening.

items.title: Gestational Surrogacy in Brazil: A Position Statement of the Brazilian Association of Assisted Reproduction (SBRA).
items.key: SBRA opposes simultaneous surrogacy arrange-ments because they are incompatible with the altruistic na-ture of the practice and supports gradual, age-appropriate disclosure of the child's gestational origin. Legal challenges include the absence of statutory regulation, cross-border reproductive tourism, and the child's right to know their origins. Continuous psychological support for all parties is mandatory and central to favorable long-term outcomes. Gestational surrogacy is a valid reproductive option for se-lected patients but requires rigorous oversight and must prioritize the best interests of the child within the Brazilian regulatory framework.

items.title: Association of short interpregnancy interval with low birth weight and preterm birth in Ethiopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
